(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 131 
SECTION 302 – SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
SECTION 302 
SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
(NEWLY CONSTRUCTED, ADDITIONS, ALTERATIONS) 
 
302.1 [Section 150.0] General. 
Single-family residential building envelopes shall comply with the applicable requirements of Section 
302. 
NOTE: The requirements of Sections 302.2 through 302.4 apply to newly constructed buildings. 
Sections 302.2 and 302.5 apply to additions or alterations. 
 
302.2 [Section 150.0] Mandatory requirements (Newly Constructed, Additions, Alterations). 
302.2.1 [Section 150.0(a)] Roof deck, ceiling and rafter roof insulation. 
The opaque portions of roof decks separating attic spaces from ambient air, and ceilings or rafter 
roofs separating conditioned spaces from unconditioned spaces or ambient air, shall meet the 
requirements below: 
302.2.1.1 [Section 150.0(a)1] Attics above conditioned space. 
In Climate Zones 4 and 8 through 16, roof decks in newly constructed attics that are above 
conditioned space shall be insulated to achieve an area-weighted average U-factor not 
exceeding U-0.184. 
Exception 1 to Section 302.2.1.1: The space-conditioning system air handler and ducts are 
located entirely in conditioned space below the ceiling separating the occupiable space from 
the attic; or 
The space-conditioning system air handler is located in unconditioned space and has 12 linear 
feet or less of supply duct, including the length of the air handler and the plenum, located in 
unconditioned space, with all other portions of the supply ducts located in conditioned space 
below the ceiling separating the occupiable space from the attic; or 
The space-conditioning system is a ductless system. 
Exception 2 to Section 302.2.1.1: Space-conditioning duct systems buried within insulation in 
an attic that complies using Sections 102.5.2 and 102.5.5 [Section 150.1(b)] and is verified 
according to RA 3.1.4.1. 
302.2.1.2 [Section 150.0(a)2] Ceilings and rafter roofs. 
Ceilings and rafter roofs shall be insulated to achieve an area-weighted average U-factor not 
exceeding U-0.043 or shall be insulated between wood-framing members with insulation 
resulting in an installed thermal resistance of R-22 or greater for the insulation alone. For 

Page 132 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 302 – SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
vented attics, the mandatory insulation shall be installed at the ceiling level; for unvented 
attics, the mandatory insulation shall be placed at either ceiling or roof level. 
Exception to Section 302.2.1.2: Ceilings and rafter roofs in an alteration shall be insulated to 
achieve an area-weighted average U-factor not exceeding 0.054 or shall be insulated between 
wood-framing members with insulation resulting in an installed thermal resistance of R-19 or 
greater. 
302.2.1.3 [Section 150.0(a)3] Attic access doors. 
Attic access doors shall have permanently attached insulation using adhesive or mechanical 
fasteners. The attic access shall be gasketed to prevent air leakage. 
302.2.1.4 [Section 150.0(a)4] Insulation placement. 
Insulation shall be installed in direct contact with a roof or ceiling which is sealed to limit 
infiltration and exfiltration as specified in Section 300.2 [Section 110.7], including but not 
limited to placing insulation either above or below the roof deck or on top of a drywall ceiling. 
302.2.2 [Section 150.0(b)] Loose-fill insulation. 
When loose-fill insulation is installed, the minimum installed weight per square foot shall conform 
with the insulation manufacturer’s installed design weight per square foot at the manufacturer’s 
labeled R-value. 
302.2.3 [Section 150.0(c)] Wall insulation. 
Opaque portions of above grade walls separating conditioned spaces from unconditioned spaces 
or ambient air shall meet the requirements of this section. 
In wood framed assemblies, compliance with U-factors may be demonstrated by installing wall 
insulation with an R-value of R-15 in 2x4 assemblies and R-21 in 2x6 assemblies, with 16 inches on 
center spacing. 
302.2.3.1 [Section 150.0(c)1] 2 x 4 inch framing. 
2 × 4 inch framing shall have an overall assembly U-factor not exceeding U-0.095. 
302.2.3.2 [Section 150.0(c)2] 2 x 6 inch framing. 
2 × 6 inch or greater framing shall have an overall assembly U-factor not exceeding U-0.069. 
302.2.3.3 [Section 150.0(c)3] Opaque non-framed assemblies. 
Opaque non-framed assemblies shall have an overall assembly U-factor not exceeding U-
0.102. 
302.2.3.4 [Section 150.0(c)4] Bay or bow window roofs and floors. 
Bay or bow window roofs and floors shall be insulated to meet the wall insulation 
requirements of Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A]. 
302.2.3.5 [Section 150.0(c)5] Masonry/Mass walls. 
Masonry/Mass walls shall be insulated to meet the wall insulation requirements of Table 
302.3-A [Table 150.1-A]. 
302.2.4 [Section 150.0(d)] Raised-floor insulation. 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 133 
SECTION 302 – SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
Raised floors separating conditioned space from unconditioned space or ambient air shall have an 
overall assembly U-factor not exceeding U-0.037. In a wood framed assembly, compliance with 
the U-factor may be demonstrated by installing insulation with an R-value of 19 or greater. 
Exception to Section 302.2.4: A building with a controlled ventilation or unvented crawlspace 
may omit raised floor insulation if all of the following are met: 
1. The foundation walls are insulated to meet the wall insulation minimums as shown in Table 
302.3-A [Table 150.1-A]; and 
2. A Class I or Class II vapor retarder is placed over the entire floor of the crawl space; and 
3. Vents between the crawl space and outside air are fitted with automatically operated louvers 
that are temperature actuated; and 
4. The requirements in Reference Residential Appendix RA4.5.1. 
302.2.5 [Section 150.0(f)] Slab edge insulation. 
Material used for slab edge insulation shall meet the following minimum specifications: 
1. Water absorption rate for the insulation material alone without facings no greater than 0.3 
percent when tested in accordance with Test Method A – 24-Hour-Immersion of ASTM C272. 
2. Water vapor permeance no greater than 2.0 perm/inch when tested in accordance with ASTM 
E96. 
3. Concrete slab perimeter insulation shall be protected from physical damage and ultraviolet 
light deterioration. 
4. Insulation for a heated slab floor shall meet the requirements of Section 300.3.5 [Section 
110.8(g)]. 
302.2.6 [Section 150.0(g)] Vapor retarder. 
In Climate Zones 1–16, the earth floor of unvented crawl space shall be covered with a Class I or 
Class II vapor retarder. This requirement shall also apply to controlled ventilation crawl space for 
buildings complying with the Exception to Section 302.2.4 [Section 150.0(d)]. 
In Climate Zones 14 and 16, a Class I or Class II vapor retarder shall be installed on the conditioned 
space side of all insulation in all exterior walls, vented attics and unvented attics with air-
permeable insulation. 
302.2.7 [Section 150.0(q)] Fenestration products. 
Fenestration, including skylight products, separating conditioned space from unconditioned space 
or outdoors shall have a maximum weighted average U-factor of 0.40. 
Exception 1 to Section 302.2.7: Up to 10 square feet of fenestration area or 0.5 percent of the 
conditioned floor area, whichever is greater, is not required to comply with the maximum U-
factor requirement. 
Exception 2 to Section 302.2.7: For dual-glazed greenhouse or garden windows, up to 30 square 
feet of fenestration area is not required to comply with the maximum U-factor requirement. 
Exception 3 to Section 302.2.7: Fenestration installed in buildings meeting Part 7 of the California 
Building Code, California Wildland-Urban Interface Code, where the building is located in Fire 

Page 134 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 302 – SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
Hazard Severity Zones or Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) Fire Areas as designated by the local 
enforcement agency. 
 
302.3 [Section 150.1] Prescriptive requirements (Newly Constructed). 
302.3.1 [Section 150.1(c)1] Insulation. 
Exception to Section 302.3.1: The insulation requirements of Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A] may 
also be met by ceiling, roof deck, wall, or floor assemblies that meet the required maximum U-
factors using a U-factor calculation method that considers the thermal effects of all elements of 
the assembly and is approved by the Executive Director. 
302.3.1.1 [Section 150.1(c)1A] Roof and ceiling insulation. 
Roof and ceiling insulation shall be installed with an R-value equal to or greater than that 
shown in Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A] meeting options A, B, or C below. 
302.3.1.1.1 [Section 150.1(c)1Ai] Option A. 
Reserved. 
302.3.1.1.2 [Section 150.1(c)1Aii] Option B. 
A minimum R-value of insulation in a ventilated attic installed between the roof rafters in 
contact with the roof deck and an additional layer of ceiling insulation located between 
the attic and the conditioned space when meeting Section 402.3.3.1 [Section 150.1(c)9A]; 
or 
302.3.1.1.3 [Section 150.1(c)1Aiii] Option C. 
A minimum R-value of ceiling insulation located between a ventilated attic and the 
conditioned space or within a cathedral ceiling assembly shall comply with Section 
402.3.3.2 [Section 150.1(c)9B]. 
302.3.1.2 [Section 150.1(c)1B] Wall insulation. 
1. Framed exterior walls. Framed exterior walls shall be insulated such that the exterior wall 
has an assembly U-factor equal to or less than that shown in Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-
A]. The U-factors shown are maximum U-factors for the exterior wall assembly. 
2. Mass walls. Mass walls above grade and below grade shall be insulated such that the wall 
has an assembly U-factor equal to or less than that shown in Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-
A], or walls shall be insulated with continuous insulation that has an R-value equal to or 
greater than that shown in Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A]. “Interior” denotes continuous 
insulation installed on the inside surface of the wall, and “exterior” denotes continuous 
insulation installed on the outside surface of the wall. 
3. Other unframed walls. Other unframed exterior walls, excluding mass walls, shall meet 
the requirements for framed walls shown in Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A]. 
302.3.1.3 [Section 150.1(c)1C] Raised-floor insulation. 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 135 
SECTION 302 – SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
Raised-floors shall be insulated such that the floor assembly has an assembly U-factor equal 
to or less than shown in Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A], or shall be insulated between wood 
framing with insulation having an R-value equal to or greater than that shown in Table 302.3-
A [Table 150.1-A]. 
Exception to Section 302.3.1.3: Raised-floor insulation may be omitted if the foundation walls 
are insulated to meet the wall insulation minimums shown in Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A], 
and a vapor retarder is placed over the entire floor of the crawl space, and the vents are fitted 
with automatically operated louvers, and the requirements of Reference Residential Appendix 
RA4.5.1 are met. 
302.3.1.4 [Section 150.1(c)1D] Slab floor perimeter insulation. 
Slab floor perimeter insulation shall be installed with a U-factor equal to or less than, or R-
value equal to or greater than shown in Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A]. The minimum depth of 
concrete-slab floor perimeter insulation shall be 16 inches or the depth of the footing of the 
building, whichever is less. 
302.3.1.5 [Section 150.1(c)1E] Quality Insulation Installation(QII). 
All buildings shall comply with the Quality Insulation Installation (QII) requirements shown in 
Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A]. When QII is required, insulation installation shall meet the 
criteria specified in Reference Appendix RA3.5. 
302.3.2 [Section 150.1(c)2] Radiant barrier. 
A radiant barrier required in Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A] shall meet the requirements specified 
in Section 300.3.8 [Section 110.8(j)], and shall meet the installation criteria specified in the 
Reference Residential Appendix RA4. 
302.3.3 [Section 150.1(c)3] Fenestration. 
302.3.3.1 [Section 150.1(c)3A] U-Factor and Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (SHGC). 
Installed fenestration products, including glazed doors, shall have an area-weighted average 
U-factor and Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (SHGC) meeting the applicable fenestration value in 
Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A] and shall be determined in accordance with Sections 300.1.1.2 
[Section 110.6(a)2] and 300.1.1.3 [Section 110.6(a)3]. 
Exception 1 to Section 302.3.3.1: New dwelling units with a conditioned floor area of 500 
square feet or less in Climate Zone 5 may comply with a maximum U-factor of 0.30. 
Exception 2 to Section 302.3.3.1: For each dwelling unit, up to 3 square feet of glazing area 
installed in doors and up to 3 square feet of tubular skylights area with dual-pane diffusers 
shall not be required to meet the U-factor and SHGC requirements of Table 302.3-A [Table 
150.1-A]. 
Exception 3 to Section 302.3.3.1: In Climate Zones 2, 4, and 6 through 15, for each dwelling 
unit up to 16 square feet of skylight area with a maximum U-factor of 0.40 and a maximum 
SHGC of 0.30. In Climate Zones 1, 3, 5, and 16 there is no SHGC requirement. 
Exception 4 to Section 302.3.3.1: For fenestration containing chromogenic type glazing: 

Page 136 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 302 – SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
1. The lower-rated labeled U-factor and SHGC shall be used with automatic controls to 
modulate the amount of solar gain and light transmitted into the space in multiple steps 
in response to daylight levels or solar intensity; 
2. Chromogenic glazing shall be considered separately from other fenestration; and 
3. Area-weighted averaging with other fenestration that is not chromatic shall not be 
permitted and shall be determined in accordance with Section 300.1.1 [Section 110.6(a)]. 
Exception 5 to Section 302.3.3.1: For dwelling units containing unrated site-built fenestration 
that meets the maximum area restriction, the U-factor and SHGC can be determined in 
accordance with the Nonresidential Reference Appendix NA6 or use default values in Table 
300.1-A [Table 110.6-A] and Table 300.1-B [Table 110.6-B]. 
302.3.3.2 [Section 150.1(c)3B] Maximum total fenestration area. 
The maximum total fenestration area shall not exceed the percentage of conditioned floor 
area, CFA, as indicated in Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A]. Total fenestration includes skylights 
and west-facing glazing. 
302.3.3.3 [Section 150.1(c)3C] Maximum West-facing fenestration area. 
The maximum west-facing fenestration area shall not exceed the percentage of conditioned 
floor area as indicated in Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A]. West-facing fenestration area 
includes skylights tilted in any direction when the pitch is less than 1:12. 
302.3.4 [Section 150.1(c)4] Shading. 
Where Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A] requires a maximum SHGC, the shading requirements shall 
be met by one of the following: 
302.3.4.1 [Section 150.1(c)4A] Maximum SHGC. 
Complying with the required maximum SHGC pursuant to Section 302.3.3.1 [Section 
150.1(c)3A]; or 
302.3.4.2 [Section 150.1(c)4B] Exterior shading device. 
An exterior operable shading louver or other exterior shading device that meets the required 
maximum SHGC; or 
302.3.4.2.1 [Section 150.1(c)4E] Permanent installation. 
Exterior shading devices must be permanently secured with attachments or fasteners that 
are not intended for removal. 
Exception to Section 302.3.4.2.1: Where the California Building Code (CBC) requires 
emergency egress or where compliance would conflict with health and safety regulations. 
302.3.4.3 [Section 150.1(c)4C] Combination SHGC and exterior shading device. 
A combination of Sections 302.3.4.1 and 302.3.4.2 to achieve the same performance as 
achieved in Section 302.3.3.1 [Section 150.1(c)3A]. 
302.3.4.4 [Section 150.1(c)4D] Overhangs for south-facing glazing. 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 137 
SECTION 302 – SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
For south-facing glazing only, optimal overhangs shall be installed so that the south-facing 
glazing is fully shaded at solar noon on August 21 and substantially exposed to direct sunlight 
at solar noon on December 21. 
302.3.5 [Section 150.1(c)5] Doors. 
Installed swinging door products separating conditioned space from outside or adjacent 
unconditioned space, but not including glazed door products, shall have an area-weighted 
average U-factor no greater than the applicable door value in Table 302.3-A [Table 150.1-A] and 
shall be determined in accordance with Section 300.1.1.2 [Section 110.6(a)2]. Glazed door 
products are treated as fenestration products in Section 302.3.3 [Sections 150.1(c)3] and Section 
302.3.4 [Section 150.1(c)4]. 
Exception to Section 302.3.5: Swinging doors between the garage and conditioned space that are 
required to have fire protection are not required to meet the applicable door value in Table 
302.3-A [Table 150.1-A].

302.3.7 [Section 150.1(c)11] Roofing products.

emittance or SRI. 
302.3.7.1 [Section 150.1(c)11A] Steep-sloped roofs in climate zones 10 through 15. 
Steep-sloped roofs in climate zones 10 through 15 shall have:

2. A minimum SRI of 16. 
302.3.7.2 [Section 150.1(c)11B] Low-sloped roofs in climate zones 13 and 15. 
Low-sloped roofs in climate zones 13 and 15 shall have: 
1. A minimum aged solar reflectance of 0.63 and a minimum thermal emittance of 0.75 or 
2. A minimum SRI of 75. 
 
302.4 [Section 100.2] Performance requirements (Newly Constructed). 
A building complies with the performance standards compliance approach as described in Section 
102 if the energy consumption calculated for the proposed design building is no greater than the 
energy budget calculated for the standard design building using Commission-certified compliance 
software as specified by the Alternative Calculation Methods Reference Manual.

302.5.1.2 [Section 150.2(a)1] Prescriptive requirements (Additions). 
302.5.1.2.1 [Section 150.2(a)1A] Additions greater than 700 square feet. 
Additions that are greater than 700 square feet shall meet the requirements of Section 
302.3 [Section 150.1(c)], with the following modifications: 
1. Extensions of existing wood-framed walls may retain the dimensions of the existing 
walls and shall install cavity insulation of R-15 in a 2x4 framing and R-21 in a 2x6 
framing. 
2. The maximum allowed fenestration area shall be the greater of 175 square feet or 20 
percent of the addition floor area, and the maximum allowed west-facing fenestration 
area shall be the greater of 70 square feet or the requirements of Section 302.3 
[Section 150.1(c)]. 
3. Alterations that add fenestration area shall have a Maximum SHGC value of 0.23 in 
Climate Zone 15. 
4. When existing siding of a wood-framed wall is not being removed or replaced, cavity 
insulation of R-15 in a 2x4 framing and R-21 in a 2x6 framing shall be installed and 
continuous insulation is not required. 
5. Additions that consist of the conversion of existing spaces from unconditioned to 
conditioned space shall not be required to perform the following as part of QII: 
5.1. Existing window and door headers shall not be required to be insulated. 
5.2. Air sealing shall not be required when the existing air barrier is not being removed 
or replaced. 
302.5.1.2.2 [Section 150.2(a)1B] Additions 700 square feet or less. 
Additions that are 700 square feet or less shall meet the requirements of Section 302.3 
[Section 150.1(c)], with the following modifications: 
1. Roof and ceiling insulation in a ventilated attic shall meet one of the following 
requirements: 
1.1. In Climate Zones 1, 2, 4, and 8 through 16, achieve an overall assembly U-factor 
not exceeding 0.025. In wood framed assemblies, compliance with U-factors may 
be demonstrated by installing insulation with an R-value of R-38 or greater. 
1.2. In Climate Zones 3, and 5 through 7, achieve an overall assembly U-factor not 
exceeding 0.031. In wood framed assemblies, compliance with U-factors may be 
demonstrated by installing insulation with an R-value of R-30 or greater. 
2. Radiant barriers shall be installed in climate zones 2-15.

framing. 
4. In Climate Zones 2, 4 and 6-15; the maximum allowed west-facing fenestration area

SECTION 303 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
SECTION 303 
MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
(NEWLY CONSTRUCTED, ADDITIONS, ALTERATIONS) 
 
303.1 [Section 160.0] General. 
Multifamily building envelopes shall comply with the applicable requirements of Section 303. Section 
303 applies to dwelling units and common use areas in multifamily buildings. Nonresidential 
occupancies in a mixed occupancy building shall comply with nonresidential requirements in Section 
301. 
NOTE: The requirements of Sections 303.2 through 303.4 apply to newly constructed buildings. 
Sections 303.2 and 303.5 apply to additions or alterations. 
 
303.2 [Section 160.1] Mandatory requirements (Newly Constructed, Additions, Alterations). 
303.2.1 [Section 160.1(a)] Ceiling and roof insulation. 
The opaque portions of ceilings and roofs separating conditioned spaces from unconditioned spaces 
or ambient air shall meet the requirements of Section 303.2.1.1 or 303.2.1.2, and Section 
303.2.1.3. 
303.2.1.1 [Section 160.1(a)1] Attic roof. 
Roofs with an attic space shall meet the requirements of 1 through 3 below: 
1. Shall be insulated to achieve an area-weighted average U-factor not exceeding U-0.043 or 
shall be insulated between wood-framing members with insulation resulting in an installed 
thermal resistance of R-22 or greater for the insulation alone. For vented attics, the 
mandatory insulation shall be installed at the ceiling level; for unvented attics, the 
mandatory insulation shall be placed at either ceiling or roof level; 
2. Attic access doors shall have permanently attached insulation using adhesive or mechanical 
fasteners. The attic access shall be gasketed to prevent air leakage; and 
3. When loose-fill insulation is installed, the minimum installed weight per square foot shall 
conform with the insulation manufacturer's installed design weight per square foot at the 
manufacturer's labeled R-value. 
303.2.1.2 [Section 160.1(a)2] Non-attic roof. 
Roofs without attic spaces shall meet the applicable requirements below: 
1. Metal building. The area-weighted average U-factor of the roof assembly shall not exceed 
0.098. 

Page 150 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 303 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
2. Wood framed and others. The area-weighted average U-factor of the roof assembly shall 
not exceed 0.075. 
303.2.1.2.1 [Section 160.1(a)2C] Insulation placement. 
When insulation is installed at the roof, fixed vents or openings to the outdoors or to 
unconditioned spaces shall not be installed. When the space between the ceiling and the 
roof is either directly or indirectly conditioned space, it shall not be considered an attic for 
the purposes of complying with CBC attic ventilation requirements. 
Exception to Section 303.2.1.2.1: Vents that do not penetrate the roof deck and are instead 
designed for wind resistance for roof membranes are not within the scope of Section 
303.2.1.2.1. 
303.2.1.3 [Section 160.1(a)3] Insulation placement. 
Insulation shall be installed in direct contact with a roof or ceiling that is sealed to limit 
infiltration and exfiltration as specified in Section 300.2 [Section 110.7], including but not 
limited to placing insulation either above or below the roof deck or on top of a drywall ceiling. 
303.2.2 [Section 160.1(b)] Wall insulation. 
Opaque portions of above grade walls separating conditioned spaces from unconditioned spaces or 
ambient air shall meet the following applicable requirements: 
1. Metal building. The area-weighted average U-factor of the wall assembly shall not exceed 
0.113. 
2. Metal framed. The area-weighted average U-factor of the wall assembly shall not exceed 
0.151. 
3. Wood framed and others. 
3.1. Nominal 2x4 inch framing shall have an area-weighted average U-factor of the wall 
assembly not exceeding 0.095. 
3.2. Nominal 2x6 inch framing shall have an area-weighted average U-factor of the wall 
assembly not exceeding 0.069. 
3.3. Other wall assemblies shall have an area-weighted average U-factor of the wall assembly 
not exceeding 0.102. 
4. Light mass walls. A 6 inch or greater hollow core concrete masonry unit shall have a U-factor 
not to exceed 0.440. 
5. Heavy mass walls. An 8 inch or greater hollow core concrete masonry unit shall have a U-factor 
not to exceed 0.690. 
6. Spandrel panels and curtain wall. The area-weighted average U-factor of the spandrel panels 
and curtain wall assembly shall not exceed 0.280. 
7. Demising walls. The opaque portions of framed demising walls shall meet the requirements 
below: 
7.1. Wood framed walls shall be insulated to meet a U-factor not greater than 0.099. 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 151 
SECTION 303 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
7.2. Metal framed walls shall be insulated to meet a U-factor not greater than 0.151. 
8. Bay or Bow windows. Bay or bow window roofs and floors shall be insulated to meet the wall 
insulation requirements of Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. 
303.2.3 [Section 160.1(c)] Floor and soffit insulation. 
The opaque portions of floors and soffits that separate conditioned spaces from unconditioned 
spaces or ambient air shall meet the applicable requirements below: 
1. Raised mass floors. Raised mass floors shall have a minimum of 3 inches of lightweight 
concrete over a metal deck or the area-weighted average U-factor of the floor assembly shall 
not exceed 0.269. 
2. Raised wood floors. Raised wood floor shall have an overall assembly U-factor not exceeding 
0.037. In a wood framed assembly, compliance with the U-factor may be demonstrated by 
installing insulation with an R-value of 19 or greater. 
3. Other floors. The area-weighted average U-factor of the floor assembly shall not exceed 0.071. 
4. Heated slab on grade floor. A heated slab on grade floor shall be insulated to meet the 
requirements of Section 300.3.5 [Section 110.8(g)]. 
Exception to Section 303.2.3: A building with a controlled ventilation or unvented crawl space may 
omit raised floor insulation if all of the following are met: 
1. The foundation walls are insulated to meet the wall insulation minimums as shown in Table 
303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]; and 
2. A Class I or Class II vapor retarder is placed over the entire floor of the crawl space; and 
3. Vents between the crawl space and outside air are fitted with automatically operated louvers 
that are temperature actuated; and 
4. The requirements in Reference Residential Appendix RA4.5.1. 
303.2.4 [Section 160.1(d)] Vapor retarder. 
In Climate Zones 1–16, the earth floor of unvented crawl space shall be covered with a Class I or 
Class II vapor retarder. This requirement shall also apply to controlled ventilation crawl space for 
buildings complying with the Exception to Section 303.2.3 [Section 160.1(c)]. 
In Climate Zones 14 and 16, a Class I or Class II vapor retarder shall be installed on the conditioned 
space side of all insulation in all exterior walls, vented attics and unvented attics with air-
permeable insulation. 
303.2.5 [Section 160.1(e)] Fenestration products. 
Fenestration separating conditioned space from unconditioned space or outdoors shall meet the 
requirements of either Section 303.2.5.1 or 303.2.5.2. 
Exception to Section 303.2.5: Fenestration installed in buildings meeting Part 7 of the California 
Building Code, California Wildland-Urban Interface Code, where the building is located in Fire 
Hazard Severity Zones or Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) Fire Areas as designated by the local 
enforcement agency. 

Page 152 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 303 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
303.2.5.1 [Section 160.1(e)1] Maximum U-factor of fenestration products. 
Fenestration, including skylight products, must have a maximum U-factor of 0.58. 
Exception 1 to Section 303.2.5.1: Up to 0.5 percent of the conditioned floor area is not 
required to comply with the maximum U-factor requirement. 
Exception 2 to Section 303.2.5.1: For dual-glazed greenhouse or garden windows, up to 30 
square feet of fenestration area per dwelling unit is not required to comply with the maximum 
U-factor requirement. 
303.2.5.2 [Section 160.1(e)2] Maximum area-weighted average U-factor. 
The area-weighted average U-factor of all fenestration, including skylight products, shall not 
exceed 0.58. 
303.2.6 [Section 160.1(g)] Slab edge Insulation. 
Slab edge insulation shall meet the following minimum specifications: 
1. Insulation material alone without the facing shall have a water absorption rate no greater than 
0.3 percent when tested in accordance with ASTM C272, Test Method A – 24-Hour-Immersion; 
and 
2. Water vapor permeance no greater than 2.0 perm/inch when tested in accordance with ASTM 
C272; and 
3. Concrete slab perimeter insulation shall be protected from physical damage and ultraviolet 
light deterioration; and 
4. Insulation for a heated slab floor shall meet the requirements of Section 300.3.5 [Section 
110.8(g)]. 
 
303.3 [Section 170.2] Prescriptive requirements (Newly Constructed) 
303.3.1 [Section 170.2(a)] Envelope component requirements. 
Exception to Section 303.3.1: The insulation requirements of Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A] may be 
met by ceiling, roof deck, wall or floor assemblies that meet the required maximum U-factors using 
a U-factor calculation method that considers the thermal effects of all elements of the assembly 
and is approved by the Executive Director. 
303.3.1.1 [Section 170.2(a)1] Exterior roofs and ceilings. 
Exterior roofs and ceilings shall comply with each of the applicable requirements in this 
subsection: 
303.3.1.1.1 [Section 170.2(a)1A] Roofing products. 
All roofing products shall meet the requirements of Section 300.3 [Section 110.8] and the 
applicable minimum aged solar reflectance and thermal emittance requirements of Table 
303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 153 
SECTION 303 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
Exception 1 to Section 303.3.1.1.1: Roof area covered with building integrated photovoltaic 
panels and building integrated solar thermal panels are not required to comply with the 
minimum requirements for solar reflectance and thermal emittance or SRI. 
Exception 2 to Section 303.3.1.1.1: Roof constructions with a weight of at least 25 lb/ft² are 
not required to comply with the minimum requirements for solar reflectance and thermal 
emittance or SRI. 
303.3.1.1.2 [Section 170.2(a)1B] Roof insulation. 
Roofs shall have an overall assembly U-factor no greater than the applicable value in Table 
303.3-A [Table 170.2-A], meeting options A, B, C or D below. Where required by Section 
300.3 [Section 110.8] and Section 303.2.1 [Section160.1(a)], insulation shall be placed in 
direct contact with a continuous roof or drywall ceiling. 
Option A: Reserved. 
Option B: A minimum R-value of insulation installed between the roof rafters in contact 
with the roof deck and an additional layer of ceiling insulation located between the attic 
and the conditioned space when meeting Section 403.3.1.2.2.1 [Section 170.2(c)3Biia]; 
or 
Option C: A minimum R-value of ceiling insulation located between the attic and the 
conditioned space when meeting Section 403.3.1.2.2.2 [Section 170.2(c)3Biib]. 
Option D: A minimum U-factor for roof assemblies above conditioned space without 
attic space. 
303.3.1.1.3 [Section 170.2(a)1C] Radiant barrier. 
A radiant barrier required in Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A] shall meet the requirements 
specified in Section 300.3.8 [Section 110.8(j)] and shall meet the installation criteria 
specified in Reference Residential Appendix RA4. 
303.3.1.2 [Section 170.2(a)2] Wall insulation. 
Exterior walls. Exterior walls shall have an overall assembly U-factor no greater than the 
applicable value in Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. 
Demising walls. Demising walls shall meet the requirements of Section 303.2.2 [Section 
160.1(b)7]. Vertical windows in demising walls between conditioned and unconditioned spaces 
shall have an area-weighted average U-factor no greater than the applicable value in Table 
303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. 
303.3.1.3 [Section 170.2(a)3A] Vertical fenestration and glazed doors in exterior walls. 
303.3.1.3.1 [Section 170.2(a)3Ai] Percent fenestration area. 
Percent fenestration area shall be limited in accordance with the applicable requirements 
of 1 and 2 below: 
1. A total fenestration area no greater than 20 percent of the conditioned floor area; and 
2. A total fenestration area no greater than 40 percent of the gross exterior wall area. 

Page 154 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 303 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
NOTE: Demising walls are not exterior walls, and therefore demising wall area is not part of 
the gross exterior wall area, and fenestration in demising walls is not part of the 
fenestration area limitation. 
303.3.1.3.2 [Section 170.2(a)3Aii] Fenestration properties. 
Installed fenestration products, including glazed doors, shall have an area-weighted average 
U-factor, Relative Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (RSHGC), and Visible Transmittance (VT) 
meeting the applicable fenestration values in Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A] and shall be 
determined in accordance with Section 300.1.1.2 [Section 110.6(a)2] and Section 300.1.1.3 
[Section 110.6(a)3]. 
Vertical fenestration in demising walls between conditioned and unconditioned spaces is 
only required to comply with the area-weighted average U-factor requirement in Table 
303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. 
Exception 1 to Section 303.3.1.3.2: For each dwelling unit, up to 3 square feet of new 
glazing area installed in doors shall not be required to meet the U-factor and RSHGC 
requirements of Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. 
Exception 2 to Section 303.3.1.3.2: For fenestration containing chromogenic type glazing: 
1. The lower-rated labeled U-factor and SHGC shall be used with automatic controls to 
modulate the amount of solar gain and light transmitted into the space in multiple steps 
in response to daylight levels or solar intensity; 
2. Chromogenic glazing shall be considered separately from other fenestration; and 
3. Area-weighted averaging with other fenestration that is not chromatic shall not be 
permitted and shall be determined in accordance with Section 300.1.1 [Section 
110.6(a)]. 
Exception 3 to Section 303.3.1.3.2: For dwelling units containing unrated site-built 
fenestration that meets the maximum area restriction, the U-factor and SHGC can be 
determined in accordance with Nonresidential Reference Appendix NA6 or using default 
values in Table 300.1-A [Table 110.6-A] and Table 300.1-B [Table 110.6-B]. 
Exception 4 to Section 303.3.1.3.2: Fenestration in dwelling units of buildings in Climate 
Zones 1, 3, 5 and 16 is not required to comply with the RSHGC requirements. 
Exception 5 to Section 303.3.1.3.2: Fenestration in dwelling units is not required to comply 
with the VT requirements. 
303.3.1.3.3 [Section 170.2(a)3Aiii] Shading. 
Where Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A] requires a maximum RSHGC, the requirements shall 
be met with an area-weighted average RSHGC excluding the effects of interior shading, no 
greater than the applicable value in Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. 
For the purposes of this paragraph, the RSHGC of a vertical window shall be determined 
according to Section 303.3.1.3.3.1 or 303.3.1.3.3.2. 
303.3.1.3.3.1- The solar heat gain coefficient of the window. 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 155 
SECTION 303 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
303.3.1.3.3.2- Relative solar heat gain coefficient is calculated using Equation 303.3-A 
[Equation 170.2-A], if the window has an overhang that extends beyond each side of the 
window jamb by a distance equal to the overhang’s horizontal projection. 
Exception 1 to Section 303.3.1.3.3.2: An area-weighted average relative solar heat gain 
coefficient of 0.56 or less shall be used for windows: 
1. That are in the first story of exterior walls that form a display perimeter; and 
2. For which codes restrict the use of overhangs to shade the windows. 
Exception 2 to Section 303.3.1.3.3.2: For vertical glazing containing chromogenic type 
glazing: 
1. The lower-rated labeled RSHGC shall be used with automatic controls to modulate 
the amount of heat flow into the space in multiple steps in response to daylight 
levels or solar intensity; and 
2. Chromogenic glazing shall be considered separately from other glazing; and 
3. Area-weighted averaging with other glazing that is not chromogenic shall not be 
permitted. 
NOTE: Demising walls are not exterior walls, and therefore fenestration in demising walls is 
not subject to SHGC requirements. 
RSHGC = SHGC × [1 + a × (2.72-PF – 1) × (sin(b × Az) + c)] (Equation 303.3-A [Equation 
170.2-A])

RSHGC = Relative Solar Heat Gain Coefficient. 
SHGC = Solar Heat Gain Coefficient of the vertical fenestration. 
Az = Azimuth of the vertical fenestration I degrees. 
PF = Projection factor as calculated by Equation 301.3-C [Equation 140.3-C]. 
303.3.1.4 [Section 170.2(a)3Aiv] Vertical fenestration Visible Transmittance (VT). 
Vertical fenestration shall have an area-weighted average Visible Transmittance (VT) no less 
than the applicable value in Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A], or Equation 303.3-B [Equation 
170.2-B], as applicable. 
Exception 1 to Section 303.3.1.4: When the window’s primary and secondary sidelit daylit 
zones are completely overlapped by one or more skylit daylit zones, then the window need not 
comply with Section 303.3.1.4 [Section 170.2(a)3Aiv]. 
Exception 2 to Section 303.3.1.4: If the window’s VT is not within the scope of NFRC 200 or 
ASTM E972, then the VT shall be calculated according to Reference Nonresidential Appendix 
NA6. 
Exception 3 to Section 303.3.1.4: For vertical windows containing chromogenic type glazing: 

Page 156 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 303 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
1. The higher rated labeled VT shall be used with automatic controls to modulate the amount 
of light transmitted into the space in multiple steps in response to daylight levels or solar 
intensity; 
2. Chromogenic glazing shall be considered separately from other glazing; and 
3. Area-weighted averaging with other glazing that is not chromogenic shall not be permitted. 
Exception 4 to Section 303.3.1.4: Fenestration in dwelling units is not required to comply with 
the VT requirements. 
NOTE: Demising walls are not exterior walls, and therefore windows in demising walls are not 
subject to VT requirements. 
VT ≥ 0.11/WWR (Equation 303.3-B [Equation 170.2-B]) 
where: 
WWR = Window Wall Ratio, the ratio of (i) the total window area of the entire 
building to (ii) the total gross exterior wall area of the entire building. If the 
WWR is greater than 0.40, then 0.40 shall be used as the value for WWR in 
Equation 303.3-B [Equation 170.2-B]. 
VT = Visible Transmittance of framed window. 
303.3.1.5 [Section 170.2(a)3B] Skylights. 
303.3.1.5.1 [Section 170.2(a)3Bi] Skylight area. 
Skylights shall have an area no greater than 5 percent of the gross exterior roof area 
Skylight Roof Ratio (SRR). 
Exception to Section 303.3.1.5.1: Buildings with an atrium over 55 feet high shall have a 
skylight area no greater than 10 percent of the gross exterior roof area. 
303.3.1.5.2 [Section 170.2(a)3Bii] U-factor. 
Skylights shall have an area-weighted performance rating U-factor no greater than the 
applicable value in Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. 
Exception 1 to Section 303.3.1.5.2: For each dwelling unit up to 16 square feet of new 
skylight area with a maximum U-factor of 0.55 and a maximum SHGC of 0.30. 
Exception 2 to Section 303.3.1.5.2: For skylights containing chromogenic type glazing: 
1. The lower-rated labeled SHGC shall be used with automatic controls to modulate the 
amount of heat flow into the space in multiple steps in response to daylight levels or 
solar intensity; and 
2. Chromogenic glazing shall be considered separately from other glazing; and 
3. Area-weighted averaging with other glazing that is not chromogenic shall not be 
permitted. 
303.3.1.5.3 [Section 170.2(a)3Biii] Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (SHGC). 
Skylights shall have an area-weighted performance rating solar heat gain coefficient no 
greater than the applicable value in Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 157 
SECTION 303 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
Exception to Section 303.3.1.5.3: For skylights containing chromogenic type glazing: 
1. The lower-rated labeled SHGC shall be used with automatic controls to modulate the 
amount of heat flow into the space in multiple steps in response to daylight levels or 
solar intensity; and 
2. Chromogenic glazing shall be considered separately from other glazing; and 
3. Area-weighted averaging with other glazing that is not chromogenic shall not be 
permitted. 
303.3.1.5.4 [Section 170.2(a)3Biv] Haze value. 
Skylights shall have a glazing material or diffuser that has a measured haze value greater 
than 90 percent, determined according to ASTM D1003 or other test method approved by 
the Energy Commission. 
Exception to Section 303.3.1.5.4: Skylights designed and installed to exclude direct sunlight 
entering the occupied space by the use of fixed or automated baffles or the geometry of 
the skylight and light well. 
303.3.1.6 [Section 170.2(a)4] Exterior doors, excluding Glazed Doors. 
All exterior doors, excluding glazed doors, that separate conditioned space from unconditioned 
space or from ambient air shall have a U-factor not greater than the applicable value in Table 
303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. Glazed doors must comply with the requirements of Section 303.3.1.3 
[Section 170.2(a)3A]. 
Exception to Section 303.3.1.6: Swinging doors that are required to have fire protection are 
not required to meet the applicable door value in Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. 
303.3.1.7 [Section 170.2(a)5] Floors. 
Floors shall meet the following requirements: 
1. Raised floors. Raised floors shall be insulated such that the floor assembly has an assembly 
U-factor equal to or less than shown in Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A], or shall be insulated 
between wood framing with insulation having an R-value equal to or greater than shown in 
Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. 
2. Slab floors. Slab floors shall have perimeter insulation installed with an F-factor equal to or 
less than or R-value equal to or greater than shown in Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. The 
minimum depth of concrete slab floor perimeter insulation shall be 16 inches or the depth 
of the footing of the building, whichever is less. 
Exception to Section 303.3.1.7: Raised-floor insulation may be omitted if the foundation walls 
are insulated to meet the wall insulation minimums shown in Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. 
303.3.1.8 [Section 170.2(a)6] Quality Insulation Installation (QII). 
All buildings up to three habitable stories shall comply with the quality insulation installation 
(QII) requirements shown in Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A]. When QII is required, insulation 
installation shall meet the criteria specified in Reference Appendix RA3.5.

303.3.3 [Section 170.2(b)] Minimum daylighting requirement for large, enclosed spaces. 
In climate zones 2 through 15, conditioned enclosed spaces, and unconditioned enclosed 
spaces that are greater than 5,000 square feet and that are directly under a roof with ceiling 
heights greater than 15 feet, shall meet the following requirements: 
1. A combined total of at least 75 percent of the floor area, as determined in building floor 
plan (drawings) view, shall be within one or more of the following: 
1.1. Primary sidelit daylit zone in accordance with Section 603.2.2.2 [Section 
160.5(b)4Dib], or 
1.2. The total floor area in the space within a horizontal distance of 0.7 times the 
average ceiling height from the edge of rough opening of skylights. 
2. All skylit daylit zones and primary sidelit daylit zones shall be shown on building plans. 
3. General lighting in daylit zones shall be controlled in accordance with Section 603.2.2.2 
[Section 160.5(b)4D]. 
4. The total skylight area is at least 3 percent of the total floor area in the space within a 
horizontal distance of 0.7 times the average ceiling height from the edge of rough 
opening of skylights; or the product of the total skylight area and the average skylight 
visible transmittance is no less than 1.5 percent of the total floor area in the space within 
a horizontal distance of 0.7 times the average ceiling height from the edge of rough 
opening of skylights. 
5. All skylights shall have a glazing material or diffuser that has a measured haze value 
greater than 90 percent, tested according to ASTM D1003 (notwithstanding its scope) or 
other test method approved by the Commission. 
Exception 1 to Section 303.3.3: In buildings with unfinished interiors, future enclosed spaces 
for which there are plans to have: 
1. A floor area of less than or equal to 5,000 square feet, or 
2. Ceiling heights of less than or equal to 15 feet. 
This exception shall not be used for S-1 or S-2 (storage), or for F-1 or F-2 (factory) 
occupancies. 
Exception 2 to Section 303.3.3: Enclosed spaces having a designed general lighting system 
with a lighting power density less than 0.5 watts per square foot. 
Exception 3 to Section 303.3.3: Enclosed spaces where it is documented that permanent 
architectural features of the building, existing structures or natural objects block direct 
beam sunlight on at least half of the roof over the enclosed space for more than 1500 
daytime hours per year between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m.

303.4 [Section 100.2] Performance requirements (Newly Constructed). 
A building complies with the performance standards compliance approach as described in 
Section 102 if the energy consumption calculated for the proposed design building is no greater 
than the energy budget calculated for the standard design building using Commission-certified 
compliance software as specified by the Alternative Calculation Methods Reference Manual. 
 
303.5 [Sections 180.1, 180.2] Additions and alterations to existing buildings. 
303.5.1 [Section 180.1] Additions. 
Additions to existing multifamily buildings shall meet the mandatory requirements of 
Section 303.5.1.1, and either prescriptive requirements of Section 303.5.1.2 [Section 
180.1(a)] or performance requirements of Section 303.5.1.3 [Section 180.1(b)]. 
303.5.1.1 [Section 180.1] Mandatory requirements (Additions). 
The addition shall meet the requirements of the sections listed below: 
101 [Section 100.0(h), 110.0, 110.1, 110.5] Systems and Equipment 
300.1, 300.2, 300.3, 303.1, 303.2 [Section 110.6, 110.7, 110.8, 160.0, 160.1] 
Mandatory Requirements for Envelopes 
303.5.1.2 [Section 180.1(a)1] Prescriptive requirements (Additions). 
The envelope of the addition shall meet the applicable requirements of the sections 
listed below: 
303.3 [Section 170.2(a and b)] Prescriptive Requirements for Envelope Systems 
303.5.1.2.1 [Section 180.1(a)1A] Additions greater than 700 square feet. 
Additions that are greater than 700 square feet shall meet the requirements of 
Section 303.3.1 [Section 170.2(a)], with the following modifications: 
1. Extensions of existing wood-framed walls may retain the dimensions of the 
existing walls and shall install cavity insulation of R-15 in a 2x4 framing and R-21 
in a 2x6 framing. 
2. The maximum allowed fenestration area shall be the greater of 175 square feet 
or 20 percent of the addition floor area. 
3. When existing siding of a wood-framed wall is not being removed or replaced, 
cavity insulation of R-15 in a 2x4 framing and R-21 in a 2x6 framing shall be 
installed and continuous insulation is not required. 
4. Additions that consist of the conversion of existing spaces from unconditioned to 
conditioned space shall not be required to perform the air sealing part of QII 
when the existing air barrier is not being removed or replaced. 
303.5.1.2.2 [Section 180.1(a)1B] Additions 700 square feet or less. 

Page 166 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 303 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
Additions that are 700 square feet or less shall meet the requirements of Section 
303.3.1 [Section 170.2(a)], with the following modifications: 
1. Roof and ceiling insulation in a ventilated attic shall meet one of the following 
requirements: 
1.1. In Climate Zones 1, 2, 4, and 8 through 16, achieve an overall assembly U-
factor not exceeding 0.025. In wood framed assemblies, compliance with U-
factors may be demonstrated by installing insulation with an R-value of R-38 
or greater. 
1.2. In Climate Zones 3 and 5 through 7, achieve an overall assembly U-factor not 
exceeding 0.031. In wood framed assemblies, compliance with U-factors 
may be demonstrated by installing insulation with an R-value of R-30 or 
greater. 
2. For buildings three habitable stories or less, radiant barriers shall be installed in 
attics with exposed attic deck undersides in Climate Zones 2–15. 
3. Extensions of existing wood-framed walls may retain the dimensions of the 
existing walls and shall install cavity insulation of R-15 in a 2x4 framing and R-21 
in a 2x6 framing; and 
4. Fenestration products must meet the U-factor, RSGHC and VT requirements of 
Table 303.5-B [Table 180.2-B]. 
5. Quality Insulation Installation (QII) requirements of Section 303.3.1.8 [Section 
170.2(a)6] do not apply. 
Exception 1 to Section 303.5.1.2.2: Additions of 300 square feet or less are not 
required to comply with the roofing product requirements of Section 303.3.1.1.1 
[Section 170.2(a)1A]. 
Exception 2 to Section 303.5.1.2.2: Insulation in an enclosed rafter ceiling shall meet 
the requirements of Section 303.2.1 [Section 160.1(a)]. 
303.5.1.3 [Section 180.1(b)] Performance requirements (Additions). 
Performance calculations shall meet the requirements of Section 102 for the addition 
alone or for the existing building plus addition. 
Exception to Section 303.5.1.3: Existing structures with a minimum R-11 insulation in 
framed walls showing compliance with Section 303.5.1.3 [Section 180.1(b)] are not 
required to show compliance with Section 303.2.2 [Section 160.1(b)]. 
303.5.2 [Section 180.2] Alterations. 
Alterations to components of existing multifamily buildings, including alterations made in 
conjunction with a change in building occupancy to a multifamily occupancy, shall meet 
mandatory requirements of Section 303.5.2.1, and either prescriptive requirements of 
Section 303.5.2.2 or performance requirements of Section 303.5.2.3.

Altered envelope components in a multifamily building shall meet the requirements 
specified in the sections listed below that are applicable to the building project and the 
minimum requirements in this section. 
101 [Section 100.0(h), 110.0, 110.1, 110.5] Systems and Equipment 
300.1, 300.2, 300.3, 303.1, 303.2 [Section 110.6, 110.7, 110.8, 160.0, 160.1] 
Mandatory Requirements for Envelopes 
303.5.2.1.1 [Section 180.2(a)1] Roof/ceiling insulation. 
The opaque portions of the roof/ceiling that separate conditioned spaces from 
unconditioned spaces or ambient air shall meet the requirements of Section 
303.5.2.2.2 [Section 180.2(b)1B]. 
303.5.2.1.2 [Section 180.2(a)2] Wall insulation. 
For the altered opaque portion of walls separating conditioned spaces from 
unconditioned spaces or ambient air shall meet the applicable requirements of Items 
1 through 4 below: 
1. Metal building. A minimum of R-13 insulation between framing members, or the 
area-weighted average U-factor of the wall assembly shall not exceed U-0.113. 
2. Metal framed. A minimum of R-13 insulation between framing members, or the 
area-weighted average U-factor of the wall assembly shall not exceed U-0.217. 
3. Wood framed and others. A minimum of R-11 insulation between framing 
members, or the area-weighted average U-factor of the wall assembly shall not 
exceed U-0.110. 
4. Spandrel panels and curtain walls. A minimum of R-4, or the area-weighted 
average U-factor of the wall assembly shall not exceed U-0.280. 
Exception to Section 303.5.2.1.2: Light and heavy mass walls. 
303.5.2.1.3 [Section 180.2(a)3] Floor insulation. 
For the altered portion of raised floors that separate conditioned spaces from 
unconditioned spaces or ambient air shall meet the applicable requirements of Items 
1 through 2 below: 
1. Raised framed floors. A minimum of R-11 insulation between framing members, 
or the area-weighted average U-factor of the floor assembly shall not exceed U-
0.071. 
2. Raised mass floors. A minimum of R-6 insulation, or the area-weighted average 
U-factor of the floor assembly shall not exceed U-0.111.

SECTION 400 – MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR ALL OCCUPANCIES 
SUBCHAPTER 4 
SPACE-CONDITIONING AND VENTILATION 
SECTION 400 
MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR ALL OCCUPANCIES 
(NEWLY CONSTRUCTED, ADDITIONS, ALTERATIONS) 
 
400.1 [Section 100.0(h)] Systems and equipment. 
Part 6 limits the installation of manufactured equipment, products, and devices to those that have 
been certified as specified by sections 101.2 [Section 110.0] and 101.3 [Section 110.1]. Requirements 
for manufactured equipment, products, and devices, when not specified in Title 24 Part 6, are 
specified in California Code of Regulations, Title 20, Sections 1601-1609. 
 
400.2 [Section 110.2] Certification by manufacturers. 
Any space-conditioning equipment listed in this section may be installed only if the manufacturer has 
certified to the Commission that the equipment complies with all the applicable requirements of this 
section. 
 
400.3 [Section 110.5] Natural gas central furnaces: pilot lights prohibited. 
Any natural gas system or equipment listed below may be installed only if it does not have a 
continuously burning pilot light: 
1. Fan-type central furnaces. 
 
400.4 [Section 110.8(a), (b), (c) and (d)] Insulation. 
400.4.1 [Section 110.8(a)] Insulation certification by manufacturers. 
All insulation shall be certified by Department of Consumer Affairs, Bureau of Household Goods 
and Services that the insulation conductive thermal performance is approved pursuant to the 
California Code of Regulations, Title 24, Part 12, Chapters 12-13, Article 3, “Standards for 
Insulating Material.” 
400.4.2 [Section 110.8(b)] Installation of urea formaldehyde foam insulation. 
Urea formaldehyde foam insulation may be applied or installed only if: 
1. It is installed in exterior side walls; and 

Page 176 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 400 – MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR ALL OCCUPANCIES 
2. A 4-mil-thick plastic polyethylene vapor retarder or equivalent plastic sheathing vapor 
retarder is installed between the urea formaldehyde foam insulation and the interior space in 
all applications. 
400.4.3 [Section 110.8(c)] Flame spread rating of insulation. 
All insulating material shall be installed in compliance with the flame spread rating and smoke 
density requirements of the CBC. 
400.4.4 [Section 110.8(d)] Installation of insulation in existing buildings. 
Insulation installed on an existing duct, shall comply with the applicable requirements below. If a 
contractor installs the insulation, the contractor shall certify to the customer, in writing, that the 
insulation meets the applicable requirements below. 
1. Ducts. If insulation is installed on an existing space-conditioning duct, it shall comply with 
Section 605.0 of the CMC. 
 
400.5 [Section 110.2] Mandatory requirements for space-conditioning equipment. 
400.5.1 [Section 110.2(a)] Efficiency. 
Equipment shall meet the applicable efficiency requirements in Tables 400.5-A through 400.5-L 
[Tables 110.2-A through 110.2-L], subject to the following: 
1. If more than one efficiency standard is listed for any equipment in Tables 400.5-A through 
400.5-L [Tables 110.2-A through 110.2-L], the equipment shall meet all the applicable 
standards that are listed; and 
2. If more than one test method is listed in Tables 400.5-A through 400.5-L [Tables 110.2-A 
through 110.2-L], the equipment shall comply with the applicable efficiency standard when 
tested with each listed test method; and 
3. Where equipment serves more than one function, it shall comply with the efficiency 
standards applicable to each function; and 
4. Where a requirement is for equipment rated at its “maximum rated capacity” or “minimum 
rated capacity,” the capacity shall be as provided for and allowed by the controls, during 
steady-state operation. 
Exception 1 to Section 400.5.1: Water-cooled centrifugal water-chilling packages that are not 
designed for operation at ANSI/AHRI Standard 550/590 test conditions of 44°F leaving chilled 
water temperature and 85°F entering condenser water temperature with 3 gallons per minute 
per ton condenser water flow shall have a maximum full load kW/ton and NPLV ratings adjusted 
using the following equation: 
Adjusted maximum full-load kW/ton rating = (full- load kW/ton from Table 400.5-D)/Kadj 
Adjusted maximum NPLV rating = (IPLV from Table 400.5-D)/Kadj 
where: 
Kadj = (A) × (B) 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 177 
SECTION 400 – MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR ALL OCCUPANCIES 
A = 0.00000014592 × (LIFT)4 – 0.0000346496 × (LIFT)3 + 0.00314196 × (LIFT)2 – 0.147199 × 
(LIFT) + 3.9302 
LIFT = LvgCond – LvgEvap (°F) 
LvgCond = Full-load leaving condenser fluid temperature (°F) 
LvgEvap = Full-load leaving evaporator fluid temperature (°F) 
B = (0.0015 × LvgEvap) + 0.934 
The adjusted full-load and NPLV values are only applicable for centrifugal chillers meeting all of 
the following full-load design ranges: 
1. Minimum Leaving Evaporator Fluid Temperature: 36°F 
2. Maximum Leaving Condenser Fluid Temperature: 115°F 
3. LIFT ≥ 20°F and ≤ 80°F 
Centrifugal chillers designed to operate outside of these ranges are not covered by this exception. 
Exception 2 to Section 400.5.1: Positive displacement (air-cooled and water-cooled) chillers with 
a leaving evaporator fluid temperature higher than 32°F shall show compliance with Table 400.5-
D [Table 110.2-D] when tested or certified with water at standard rating conditions, per the 
referenced test procedure. 
Exception 3 to Section 400.5.1: Equipment primarily serving refrigerated warehouses or 
commercial refrigeration.

Footnotes to Table 400.5-E [Table 110.2-E]: 
a. For purposes of this table, open-circuit cooling tower performance is defined as the water flow rating of the tower at 
the given rated conditions divided by the fan motor nameplate power. 
b. For purposes of this table, closed-circuit cooling tower performance is defined as the process water flow rating of the 
tower at the given rated conditions divided by the sum of the fan motor nameplate rated power and the integral 
spray pump motor nameplate power. 
c. For purposes of this table dry cooler performance is defined as the process water flow rating of the unit at the given 
thermal rating condition divided by the total fan motor nameplate power of the unit and air -cooled condenser 
performance is defined as the heat rejected from the refrigerant divided by the fan motor nameplate power of the 
unit. 
d. Open cooling towers shall be tested using the test procedures in CTI ATC-105. Performance of factory assembled 
open cooling towers shall be either certified as base models as specified in CTI STD-201 or verified by testing in the 
field by a CTI approved testing agency. Open factory assembled cooling towers with custom options added to a CTI 
certified base model for the purpose of safe maintenance or to reduce environmental or noise impact shall be rated 
at 90 percent of the CTI certified performance of the associated base model or at the manufacturer’s stated 
performance, whichever is less. Base models of open factory assembled cooling towers are open cooling towers 
configured in exact accordance with the Data of Record submitted to CTI as specified by CTI STD-201. There are no 
certification requirements for field erected cooling towers. 
e. Applicable test procedure and reference year are provided under the definitions. For refrigerated warehouses or 
commercial refrigeration applications, condensers shall comply with requirements specified by Section 901.1 [Section 
120.6(a)] or Section 902.1 [Section 120.6(b)].

a. The size category is the full-load net refrigeration cooling mode capacity, which is the capacity of the evaporator available for cooling of the thermal lo ad

recover COPHR is only required at one of the four heating AHRI 550/590 (I-P) standard ratings conditions of Low, Medium, Hot-Water 1 or Hot-Water 2.

Requirements.

400.5.2 [Section 110.2(b)] Controls for heat pumps with supplementary heaters. 
Control requirements for heat pumps with supplementary heaters in single-family 
residential buildings are specified in Section 402.2.2.7 [Section 150.0(h)7] and Section 
402.2.4.2 [Section 150.0(i)2]. Heat pumps with supplementary heaters in nonresidential and 
multifamily buildings shall have controls: 
1. That prevent supplementary heater operation when the heating load can be met by the 
heat pump alone; and 
2. In which the cut-on temperature for heat pump heating is higher than the cut-on 
temperature for supplementary heating, and the cut-off temperature for heat pump 
heating is higher than the cut-off temperature for supplementary heating. 
Exception 1 to Section 400.5.2: The controls may allow supplementary heater operation 
during: 
1. Defrost; and 
2. Transient periods such as start-ups and following room thermostat setpoint advance, if 
the controls provide preferential rate control, intelligent recovery, staging, ramping or 
another control mechanism designed to preclude the unnecessary operation of 
supplementary heating. 
Exception 2 to Section 400.5.2: Room air-conditioner heat pumps. 
400.5.3 [Section 110.2(c)] Thermostats. 
All heating or cooling systems not controlled by a central energy management control 
system (EMCS) shall have a setback thermostat. 
Setback capabilities . All thermostats shall have a clock mechanism that allows the building 
occupant to program the temperature setpoints for at least four periods within 24 hours. 
Thermostats for heat pumps shall meet the requirements of Section 400.5.2 [Section 
110.2(b)]. 
Exception to Section 400.5.3: Gravity gas wall heaters, gravity floor heaters, gravity room 
heaters, noncentral electric heaters, fireplaces or decorative gas appliances, wood stoves, 
room air conditioners and room air-conditioner heat pumps. 
400.5.4 [Section 110.2(d)] Gas-fired and oil-fired furnace standby loss controls. 
All furnaces with input ratings ≥ 225,000 Btu/hr, including electric furnaces, that are not 
located within the conditioned space shall have jacket losses not exceeding 0.75 percent of 
the input rating. 
Gas-fired and oil-fired forced-air furnaces with input ratings ≥ 225,000 Btu/hr shall also have 
an intermittent ignition or interrupted device (IID), and have either power venting or a flue 
damper. A vent damper is an acceptable alternative to a flue damper for furnaces where 
combustion air is drawn from the conditioned space. 
400.5.5 [Section (110.2(e)] Open and closed-circuit cooling towers. 
All open and closed-circuit cooling tower installations shall comply with the following:

400.5.6 [Section 110.2(f)] Low leakage air -handling units . 
To qualify as a low leakage air-handling unit for use for meeting the requirements for 
applicable low leakage air-handling unit compliance credit(s) available in the performance 
standards set forth in Sections 102.5.1, 102.5.2, and 102.5.5 [Sections 150.1(b) and 140.1], 
the manufacturer shall certify to the Energy Commission that the air-handling unit meets the 
specifications in Reference Joint Appendix JA9. 
 
400.6 [Section 110.12] Mandatory requirements for demand management. 
Buildings, other than healthcare facilities, that install or are required to install demand 
responsive controls shall comply with the applicable demand responsive control requirements of 
Sections 400.6.1 and 400.6.2 [Sections 110.12(a) and 110.12(b)]. 
400.6.1 [Section 110.12(a)] Demand responsive controls. 
1. All demand responsive controls shall be either: 

Page 210 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 400 – MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR ALL OCCUPANCIES 
1.1. A certified OpenADR 2.0a or OpenADR 2.0b Virtual End Node (VEN), as specified 
under Clause 11, Conformance, in the applicable OpenADR 2.0 Specification; or a 
certified Baseline Profile OpenADR 3.0 Virtual End Node; or 
1.2. Certified to the Energy Commission as being capable of responding to a demand 
response signal from a certified OpenADR 2.0b or a certified Baseline Profile 
OpenADR 3.0 Virtual End Node by automatically implementing the control functions 
requested by the Virtual End Node for the equipment it controls. 
2. All demand responsive controls shall be capable of communicating with the VEN using a 
wired or wireless bidirectional communication protocol. 
3. When the demand response signal is disabled or unavailable, all demand responsive 
controls shall continue to perform all other control functions provided by the control. 
4. Demand responsive control thermostats shall comply with Reference Joint Appendix 5 
(JA5), Technical Specifications for Occupant Controlled Smart Thermostats. 
400.6.2 [Section 110.12(b)] Demand responsive zonal HVAC controls. 
Nonresidential HVAC systems with DDC to the Zone level shall be programmed to allow 
centralized demand shed for noncritical zones as follows: 
400.6.2.1 [Section 110.12(b)1] Operating cooling temperature setpoint. 
The controls shall have a capability to remotely increase the operating cooling 
temperature set points by 4 degrees or more in all noncritical zones on signal from a 
centralized contact or software point within an Energy Management Control System 
(EMCS). 
400.6.2.2 [Section 110.12(b)2] Operating heating temperature setpoint. 
The controls shall have a capability to remotely decrease the operating heating 
temperature set points by 4 degrees or more in all noncritical zones on signal from a 
centralized contact or software point within an EMCS. 
400.6.2.3 [Section 110.12(b)3] Remote temperature reset. 
The controls shall have capabilities to remotely reset the temperatures in all noncritical 
zones to original operating levels on signal from a centralized contact or software point 
within an EMCS. 
400.6.2.4 [Section 110.12(b)4] Adjustable rate of change. 
The controls shall be programmed to provide an adjustable rate of change for the 
temperature increase, decrease, and reset. 
400.6.2.5 [Section 110.12(b)5] Required features. 
The controls shall have the following features: 
1. Disabled. Disabled by authorized facility operators; and 
2. Manual control. Manual control by authorized facility operators to allow adjustment 
of heating and cooling set points globally from a single point in the EMCS; and 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 211 
SECTION 400 – MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR ALL OCCUPANCIES 
3. Automatic Demand Shed Control. Upon receipt of a demand response signal, the 
space-conditioning systems shall conduct a centralized demand shed, as specified in 
Section 400.6.2.1 and 400.6.2.2 [Sections 110.12(b)1 and 110.12(b)2], for noncritical 
zones during the demand response period.

SECTION 401 – NONRESIDENTIAL AND HOTEL/MOTEL OCCUPANCIES 
SECTION 401 
NONRESIDENTIAL AND HOTEL/MOTEL OCCUPANCIES 
(NEWLY CONSTRUCTED, ADDITIONS, ALTERATIONS) 
 
401.1 [Section 120.0] General. 
Section 401 establishes requirements for the design and installation of building ventilation and 
space-conditioning systems and equipment in nonresidential and hotel/motel buildings that are 
within the scope of Section 100.3 [Section 100.0(a)]. 
NOTE: The requirements of Sections 401.2 through 401.4 apply to newly constructed buildings. 
Sections 401.2 and 401.5 apply to additions or alterations to existing buildings. 
 
401.2 Mandatory requirements (Newly Constructed, Additions, Alterations). 
401.2.1 [Section 120.1] Ventilation and indoor air quality. 
All occupiable spaces in hotel/motel buildings, and nonresidential buildings other than 
healthcare facilities shall comply with the applicable requirements of Section 401.2.1.1 
through 401.2.1.5 [Section 120.1(a) through 120.1(g)]. Healthcare facilities shall be 
ventilated in accordance with Chapter 4 of the California Mechanical Code. 
The required outdoor air-ventilation rate and the air-distribution system design shall be 
clearly identified on the plans in accordance with Section 10-103 of Title 24, Part 1. 
401.2.1.1 [Section 120.1(c)] Occupiable spaces. 
All occupiable spaces shall meet the requirements of Section 401.2.1.1.1 [Section 
120.1(c)1] and shall also comply with either Section 401.2.1.1.2 [Section 120.1(c)2] or 
Section 401.2.1.1.3 [Section 120.1(c)3]. 
401.2.1.1.1 [Section 120.1(c)1] Air filtration. 
Mechanical system types specified below shall be designed to ensure that all 
recirculated air and all outdoor air supplied to the occupiable space is filtered before 
passing through any system thermal conditioning components. Air filters shall 
conform to the requirements of this section. 
1. Mechanical space-conditioning systems that supply air to an occupiable space 
through ductwork exceeding 10 ft (3 m) in length. 
2. Mechanical supply-only ventilation systems and makeup air systems that provide 
outside air to an occupiable space. 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 213 
SECTION 401 – NONRESIDENTIAL AND HOTEL/MOTEL OCCUPANCIES 
3. The supply side of mechanical balanced ventilation systems, including heat 
recovery ventilation systems and energy recovery ventilation systems that provide 
outside air to an occupiable space. 
Air filter efficiency. The filters shall have a designated efficiency equal to or greater 
than MERV 13 when tested in accordance with ASHRAE Standard 52.2, or a particle 
size efficiency rating equal to or greater than 50 percent in the 0.30–1.0 µm range, 
and equal to or greater than 85 percent in the 1.0–3.0 µm range when tested in 
accordance with AHRI Standard 680; and 
Systems shall be equipped with air filters that meet either: 
1. Nominal 2-inch minimum depth filter(s); or 
2. Nominal one inch minimum depth filter(s) shall be allowed if the filter(s) are sized 
according to Equation 401.2-A [Equation 120.1-A], based on a maximum face 
velocity of 150 feet per minute. 
Aface = Qfilter /Vface (Equation 401.2-A [Equation 120.1-A]) 
where: 
Aface = air filter face area, the product of air filter nominal length × 
nominal width, ft2 
Qfilter = design airflow rate for the air filter, ft3/min 
Vface = air filter face velocity ≤ 150, ft/min 
Air bypass prevention. Filter racks or grilles shall use gaskets, sealing or other means 
to close gaps around inserted filters and prevent air from bypassing the filter. 
Exception 1 to Section 401.2.1.1.1: Evaporative coolers are not subject to the air 
filtration requirements of Section 401.2.1.1.1 [Section 120.1(c)1]. 
Exception 2 to Section 401.2.1.1.1: For heat recovery ventilators and energy 
recovery ventilators, the location of the filters required by Section 401.2.1.1.1 
[Section 120.1(c)1A] may be downstream of a system thermal conditioning 
component, provided the system is equipped with ancillary filtration upstream of the 
system’s thermal conditioning component. 
401.2.1.1.2 [Section 120.1(c)2] Natural ventilation. 
Naturally ventilated spaces shall be designed in accordance with the following: 
1. Floor area to be ventilated. Spaces or portions of spaces to be naturally 
ventilated shall be located within a distance based on the ceiling height, as 
specified below. 
The ceiling height (H) to be used shall be the minimum ceiling height in the space, 
or for ceilings that are increasing in height as distance from the operable 
openings is increased, the ceiling height shall be determined as the average 
height of the ceiling within 20 feet from the operable opening. [ASHRAE 
62.1:6.4.1.1] 

Page 214 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 401 – NONRESIDENTIAL AND HOTEL/MOTEL OCCUPANCIES 
1.1. Single side opening. For spaces with operable opening on one side of the 
zone, the naturally ventilated area shall extend to a distance not greater than 
two times the height (H) of the ceiling from the openings. [ASHRAE 
62.1:6.4.1.3] 
1.2. Double side opening. For zones with openings on two opposite sides of the 
zone, the naturally ventilated area shall extend between the openings 
separated by a distance not greater than five times the height of the ceiling. 
[ASHRAE 62.1:6.4.1.4] 
1.3. Corner opening. For zones with operable openings on two adjacent sides of a 
zone, the naturally ventilated area shall extend to a distance not greater than 
five times the height of the ceiling along a line drawn between the outside 
edges of the two openings that are the farthest apart. The remaining area of 
the zone that is not bounded by the walls that have the openings and the line 
drawn between the openings shall comply with the requirements for Single 
side opening as having openings on only one side of the zone. [ASHRAE 
62.1:6.4.1.5] 
2. Location and size of openings. Zones or portions of zones to be naturally 
ventilated shall have a permanently open airflow path to openings directly 
connected to the outdoors. The openable area shall be not less than 4 percent of 
the net occupiable floor area. Where openings are covered with louvers or 
otherwise obstructed, the openable area shall be based on the net free 
unobstructed area through the opening. Where interior rooms, or portions of 
rooms, without direct openings to the outdoors are ventilated through adjoining 
rooms, the opening between rooms shall be permanently unobstructed and have 
a free area of not less than 8 percent of the area of the interior room or less than 
25 square feet. [ASHRAE 62.1:6.4.1.6] 
3. Control and accessibility. The means to open the required operable opening shall 
be readily accessible to building occupants whenever the space is occupied. 
Controls shall be designed to coordinate operation of the natural and mechanical 
ventilation systems. [ASHRAE 62.1:6.4.3] 
401.2.1.1.2.1- Mechanical ventilation system for naturally ventilated spaces. 
Naturally ventilated spaces shall also include a mechanical ventilation system 
designed in accordance with Section 401.2.1.1.3 [Section 120.1(c)3]. 
Exception 1 to Section 401.2.1.1.2.1: Spaces not served by a space-conditioning 
system. 
Exception 2 to Section 401.2.1.1.2.1: Spaces where natural ventilation openings 
complying with Section 401.2.1.1.2 [Section 120.1(c)2] are either permanently 
open or have controls that prevent the openings from being closed during 
periods of expected occupancy. 
401.2.1.1.3 [Section 120.1(c)3] Mechanical ventilation. 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 215 
SECTION 401 – NONRESIDENTIAL AND HOTEL/MOTEL OCCUPANCIES 
Occupiable spaces shall be ventilated with a mechanical ventilation system capable 
of providing an outdoor airflow rate to the zone (Vz) no less than Equation 401.2-B 
[Equation 120.1-F] as described below: 
Vz = The larger of Rp × Pz or Ra × Az (Equation 401.2-B [Equation 120.1-F]) 
where: 
Rp = 15 cubic feet per minute of outdoor airflow per person 
Pz = The expected number of occupants. For spaces without fixed seating, 
the expected number of occupants shall be the expected number 
specified by the building designer or the default occupancy density in 
Table 401.2-A [Table 120.1-A] times the occupiable floor area of the zone, 
whichever is greater. For spaces with fixed seating, the expected number 
of occupants shall be determined in accordance with the California 
Building Code Section 1004.6. 
Ra = The area-based minimum ventilation airflow rate in Table 401.2-A 
[Table 120.1-A]. 
Az = The net occupiable floor area of the ventilation zone in square feet. 
Exception to Section 401.2.1.1.3: The rate of outdoor air required by Section 
401.2.1.1.3 [Section 120.1(c)3] may be provided with air transferred from other 
ventilated space if: 
1. Use of transfer air is in accordance with Section 401.2.1.5 [Section 120.1(g)]; and 
2. The outdoor air that is supplied to all spaces combined, is sufficient to meet the 
requirements of Section 401.2.1.1.3 [Section 120.1(c)3] for each space 
individually.
