d. For this scenario, use of elbows is not permitted. 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 307 
SECTION 402 – SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
e. For this scenario, 4 in. (100 mm) oval duct shall be permitted, provided the minor axis of the oval is 
greater than or equal to 3 in. (75 mm) 
f. When a vented range hood utilizes a capture efficiency rating to demonstrate compliance with Section 
402.2.7.5.1 [Section 150.0(o)1Giiib], a static pressure greater than or equal to 0.25 in. of water at the 
rating point shall not be required, and the airflow listed in the approved directory corresponding to the 
compliant capture efficiency rating point shall be applied to Table 402.2-G [Table 150.0-H] for 
determining compliance. 
402.2.7.5.4 [Section 150.0(o)1Gvi] Sound ratings for local mechanical exhaust. 
Local mechanical exhaust systems shall be rated for sound in accordance with Section 7.3 
of ASHRAE 62.2 at no less than the minimum airflow rate required by Section 402.2.7.5 
[Section 150.0(o)1G]. 
Exception to Section 402.2.7.5.4: Kitchen range hoods may be rated for sound at no less 
than 100 cfm at a static pressure determined at working speed as specified in HVI 916 
section 7.2. 
402.2.7.6 [Section 150.0(o)1H] Airflow measurement of whole-dwelling unit ventilation. 
The airflow required by Section 402.2.7.3 [Section 150.0(o)1C] is the quantity of outdoor 
ventilation air supplied or indoor air exhausted by the mechanical ventilation system as 
installed and shall be measured by using a flow hood, flow grid or other airflow measuring 
device at the mechanical ventilation fan’s inlet terminals/grilles or outlet terminals/grilles in 
accordance with the procedures in Reference Residential Appendix RA3.7. Balanced 
mechanical ventilation system airflow shall be the average of the supply fan and exhaust fan 
flows. 
402.2.7.7 [Section 150.0(o)1I] Sound ratings for whole-dwelling unit ventilation systems. 
Whole-dwelling unit ventilation systems shall be rated for sound in accordance with Section 
7.3 of ASHRAE 62.2 at no less than the minimum airflow rate required by Section 402.2.7.3 
[Section 150.0(o)1C]. 
402.2.7.8 [Section 150.0(o)1J] Label for whole-dwelling unit ventilation system on-off 
control. 
Compliance with ASHRAE 62.2 Section 4.4 (Control and Operation) shall require manual ON-
OFF control switches associated with whole-dwelling unit ventilation systems to have a label 
clearly displaying the following text, or equivalent text: “This switch controls the indoor air 
quality ventilation for the home. Leave switch in the ‘on’ position at all times unless the 
outdoor air quality is very poor.” 
402.2.7.9 [Section 150.0(o)1K] Combustion air and compensating outdoor air or makeup 
air. 
All dwelling units shall conform to the applicable requirements specified in California 
Mechanical Code Chapter 7, Combustion Air. 
All dwelling units shall conform to the requirements in ASHRAE 62.2 Section 6.4, Combustion 
and Solid-Fuel-Burning Appliances. 
402.2.8 [Section 150.0(o)2] Field verification and diagnostic testing for ventilation and indoor 
air quality. 

Page 308 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 402 – SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
All dwelling units shall comply with Section 402.2.8 [Section 150.0(o)2] below. 
Whole-dwelling unit ventilation airflow performance. The whole-dwelling unit ventilation 
airflow required by Section 402.2.7.3 [Section 150.0(o)1C] shall be confirmed through field 
verification and diagnostic testing in accordance with the applicable procedures specified in 
Reference Residential Appendix RA3.7. Balanced mechanical ventilation system airflow shall be 
the average of the supply fan and exhaust fan flows. Ventilation airflow of systems with multiple 
operating modes shall be tested in all modes designed to comply with the required ventilation 
airflows. 
Kitchen local mechanical exhaust—vented range hoods. Vented range hoods installed to comply 
with local mechanical exhaust requirements specified in Section 402.2.7.5 [Section 150.0(o)1G] 
shall be field verified in accordance with the procedures in Reference Residential Appendix 
RA3.7.4.3 to confirm the model is rated by HVI or AHAM to comply with the following 
requirements: 
1. The minimum ventilation airflow rate as specified by Section 402.2.7.5 [Section 150.0(o)1G], 
or alternatively the minimum capture efficiency as specified by Section 402.2.7.5 [Section 
150.0(o)1G]. 
2. The maximum sound rating as specified in Section 402.2.7.5.4 [Section 150.0(o)1Gvi]. 
Heat recovery ventilation (HRV) and energy recovery ventilation (ERV) system fan efficacy. 
Systems with heat or energy recovery serving a single dwelling unit shall have a fan efficacy of 
≤1.0 W/cfm as confirmed by field verification in accordance with Reference Appendix RA3.7.4.4. 
 
402.3 [Section 150.1] Prescriptive Requirements (Newly Constructed). 
402.3.1 [Section 150.1(c)6] Heating system type. 
Heating system types shall be installed as required in Table 402.3-A [Table 150.1-A] in Section 
402.3.8. The space conditioning system shall be a heat pump, or shall meet the performance 
compliance requirements of Section 402.4 [Section 150.1(b)1]. 
Exception to Section 402.3.1: A supplemental heating unit may be installed in a space served 
directly or indirectly by a primary heating system, provided that the unit thermal capacity does 
not exceed 2 kW or 7,000 Btu/hr and is controlled by a time-limiting device not exceeding 30 
minutes. 
402.3.2 [Section 150.1(c)7] Space heating and space cooling. 
All space heating and space cooling equipment shall comply with minimum Appliance Efficiency 
Regulations as specified in Sections 400.1, 400.2, and 400.5 [Sections 110.0 through 110.2] and 
meet all applicable requirements of Sections 402.1, 402.2, [Sections 150.0] and 402.3.2.1 [Section 
150.1(c)7A]. 
402.3.2.1 [Section 150.1(c)7A] Refrigerant charge verification. 
When refrigerant charge verification is shown as required by Table 402.3-A [Table 150.1-A] in 
Section 402.3.8, air-cooled air conditioners and air-source heat pumps, including but not 
limited to ducted split systems, ducted packaged systems, small duct high velocity systems, 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 309 
SECTION 402 – SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
and mini-split systems, shall comply with Section 402.3.2.1.1 [Section 150.1(c)7Ai] unless the 
system is of a type that cannot be verified using the specified procedures. Systems which are 
of a type that cannot be verified using the specified procedures with the requirements of 
Section 402.3.2.1.1 [Section 150.1(c)7Ai] shall comply with Section 402.3.2.1.2 [Section 
150.1(c)7Aii] as applicable. 
Exception to Section 402.3.2.1: Packaged systems for which the manufacturer has verified 
correct system refrigerant charge prior to shipment from the factory are not required to have 
refrigerant charge confirmed through field verification and diagnostic testing. The installer of 
these packaged systems shall certify on the Certificate of Installation that the packaged 
system was pre-charged at the factory and has not been altered in a way that would affect 
the charge. Ducted systems shall comply with minimum system airflow rate requirements in 
Section 402.3.2.1.1 [Section 150.1(c)7Aib], provided that the system is of a type that can be 
verified using the procedure specified in Section RA3.3 or an approved alternative in Section 
RA1. 
402.3.2.1.1 [Section 150.1(c)7Ai] Airflow and refrigerant charge verification 
procedures. 
402.3.2.1.1.1- Measurement access hole. Have measurement access holes (MAH) 
installed according to the specifications in Reference Residential Appendix Section 
RA3.2.2.3; and 
Exception to Section 402.3.2.1.1.1: Systems that cannot conform to the specifications 
for hole location in Reference Residential Appendix Figure RA3.2-1, shall not be 
required to provide holes as described in Figure RA3.2-1. 
402.3.2.1.1.2- Minimum system airflow rate. System airflow rate in accordance with 1 
or 2 below shall be confirmed through field verification and diagnostic testing in 
accordance with all applicable procedures specified in Reference Residential Appendix 
Section RA3.3 or an approved alternative procedure as specified by Section RA1; and 
1. For small duct high velocity systems the system airflow rate shall be greater than 
or equal to 250 cfm per ton; or 
2. For all other air-cooled air conditioner or air-source heat pump systems the system 
airflow rate shall be greater than or equal to 350 cfm per ton. 
Exception to Section 402.3.2.1.1.2: Standard ducted systems without zoning dampers 
may comply with the minimum airflow rate by meeting the applicable requirements in 
Table 402.2-A or Table 402.2-B [Table 150.0-B or 150.0-C] as confirmed by field 
verification and diagnostic testing in accordance with the procedures in Reference 
Residential Appendix Section RA3.1.4.4 and RA3.1.4.5. The design clean-filter pressure 
drop requirements of Section 402.2.6.12.3 [Section 150.0(m)12D] for the system air 
filter device(s) shall conform to the requirements given in Table 402.2-A and Table 
402.2-B [Table 150.0-B and 150.0-C]. 
402.3.2.1.1.3- Refrigerant charge. The installer shall charge the system according to 
manufacturer’s specifications. Refrigerant charge shall be verified according to one of 
the following options, as applicable: 

Page 310 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 402 – SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
1. The installer and rater shall perform the standard charge procedure as specified by 
Reference Residential Appendix Section RA3.2.2, or an approved alternative 
procedure as specified by Section RA1; or 
2. The installer shall perform the weigh-in charging procedure as specified by 
Reference Residential Appendix Section RA3.2.3.1 provided the system is of a type 
that can be verified using the Section RA3.2.2 standard charge verification 
procedure and Section RA3.3 airflow rate verification procedure or approved 
alternatives in Section RA1. The ECC-Rater shall verify the charge using Sections 
RA3.2.2 and RA3.3 or approved alternatives in Section RA1. 
Exception 1 to Section 402.3.2.1.1.3: When the outdoor temperature is less than 55°F 
and the installer utilizes the weigh-in charging procedure in Reference Residential 
Appendix Section RA3.2.3.1 to verify the refrigerant charge, the installer may elect to 
utilize the verification procedure in Reference Residential Appendix Section RA3.2.3.2. 
If the verification procedure in Section RA3.2.3.2 is used for compliance, the system's 
thermostat shall conform to the specifications in Section 400.6 [Section 110.12]. 
Ducted systems shall comply with minimum system airflow rate requirement in 
Section 402.3.2.1.1.2 [Section 150.1(c)7Aib]. 
402.3.2.1.2 [Section 150.1(c)7Aii] Airflow and refrigerant charge alternate verification 
procedures. 
Systems that utilize forced air ducts shall comply with the minimum system airflow rate 
requirement in Section 402.3.2.1.1 [Section 150.1(c)7Aib] provided the system is of a type 
that can be verified using the procedures in Section RA3.3 or an approved alternative 
procedure in Section RA1. 
The installer shall confirm the refrigerant charge using the weigh-in charging procedure 
specified in Reference Residential Appendix Section RA3.2.3.1, as verified by an ECC-Rater 
according to the procedures specified in Reference Residential Appendix Section 
RA3.2.3.2. 
402.3.3 [Section 150.1(c)9] Space conditioning distribution systems. 
All space conditioning systems shall meet all applicable requirements of Section 402.3.3.1 or 
Section 402.3.3.2. 
402.3.3.1 [Section 150.1(c)9A] High performance attics. 
Air handlers or ducts are allowed to be in ventilated attic spaces when the roof and ceiling 
insulation level meet Option B in Table 402.3-A [Table 150.1-A] in Section 402.3.8. Duct 
insulation levels shall meet the requirements in Table 402.3-A [Table 150.1-A] in Section 
402.3.8. 
402.3.3.2 [Section 150.1(c)9B] Ducts and air handlers in conditioned space. 
Duct systems and air handlers of HVAC systems shall be located entirely in conditioned space, 
and confirmed through field verification and diagnostic testing to meet the criterion of 
Reference Residential Appendix RA3.1.4.3.8. Duct insulation levels shall meet the 
requirements in Table 402.3-A [Table 150.1-A] in Section 402.3.8. For dwelling units with 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 311 
SECTION 402 – SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
attics, the duct system and air handlers of HVAC systems shall be located below the ceiling 
separating the occupiable space from the attic. 
NOTE: Gas heating appliances installed in conditioned spaces must meet the combustion air 
requirements of the California Mechanical Code Chapter 7, as applicable. 
402.3.4 [Section 150.1(c)10] Central fan integrated ventilation systems. 
Central forced air system fans used to provide outside air, shall have an air-handling unit fan 
efficacy less than or equal to the maximum W/cfm specified in one of the options below. 
1. 0.45 W/cfm for gas furnace air-handling units manufactured on or after July 3, 2019. Gas 
furnace air-handling units manufactured prior to July 3, 2019 shall comply with a fan efficacy 
value less than or equal to 0.58 w/cfm as confirmed by field verification and diagnostic testing 
in accordance with the procedures given in Reference Residential Appendix RA3.3. 
2. 0.58 W/cfm for air-handling units that are not gas furnaces. 
3. 0.62 W/cfm for small duct high velocity air-handling units. 
The airflow rate and fan efficacy requirements in this section shall be confirmed through field 
verification and diagnostic testing in accordance with all applicable procedures specified in 
Reference Residential Appendix RA3.3. Central Fan integrated ventilation systems shall be 
certified to the Energy Commission as intermittent ventilation systems as specified in Reference 
Residential Appendix RA3.7.4.2. 
402.3.5 [Section 150.1(c)12] Ventilation cooling. 
Single-family homes shall comply with the Whole-house fan (WHF) requirements shown in Table 
402.3-A [Table 150.1-A] in Section 402.3.8. When a WHF is required, comply with 402.3.5.1 
through 402.3.5.3. 
Exception to Section 402.3.5: New dwelling units with a conditioned floor area of 500 square feet 
or less shall not be required to comply with the WHF requirements. 
402.3.5.1- Have installed one or more WHFs whose total airflow cfm is equal to or greater 
than 1.5 cfm/ft2 of conditioned floor area. Airflow cfm for WHF's shall be determined based 
on the airflow listed in the Home Ventilating Institute Certified Products Directory. 
402.3.5.2- Have at least 1 square foot of attic vent free area for each 750 cfm of rated whole-
house fan airflow cfm, or if the manufacturer has specified a greater free vent area, the 
manufacturers’ free vent area specifications. 
Exception to Section 402.3.5.2: WHFs that are directly vented to the outside. 
402.3.5.3- Provide homeowners who have WHFs with a one page “How to operate your 
whole-house fan” informational sheet. 
402.3.6 [Section 150.1(c)13] HVAC system bypass ducts. 
Bypass ducts that deliver conditioned supply air directly to the space conditioning system return 
duct airflow shall not be used. 
402.3.7 [Section 150.1(c)15] Ventilation System Fault Indicator Display (FID).

that is ECC-rater field verified as specified in Joint Reference Appendix JA17.

402.4 [Section 100.2] Performance requirements (Newly Constructed). 
A building complies with the performance standards compliance approach as described in Section 
102 if the energy consumption calculated for the proposed design building is no greater than the 
energy budget calculated for the standard design building using Commission-certified compliance 
software as specified by the Alternative Calculation Methods Reference Manual. 
 
402.5 [Section 150.2] Additions and alterations to existing buildings. 
402.5.1 [Section 150.2(a)] Additions. 
Additions to existing single-family residential buildings shall meet the mandatory requirements of 
Section 402.5.1.1, and either prescriptive requirements of Section 402.5.1.2 or performance 
requirements of Section 402.5.1.3 [Section 150.2(a)1 or 2]. 
Exception to Section 402.5.1: When heating or cooling will be extended to an addition from the 
existing system(s), the existing heating and cooling equipment need not comply with Part 6. The 
heating system capacity must be adequate to meet the minimum requirements of CRC 303.10. 
402.5.1.1 [Section 150.2(a)] Mandatory requirements (Additions). 
Mechanical systems and equipment shall meet the requirements of the sections listed below: 
101.2, 101.3, 101.4 [Section 110.0, 110.1, 110.5] Systems and Equipment 
400.2, 400.4.4, 400.5, 402.2.1, 402.2.2, 402.2.4, 402.2.5, 402.2.6 [Section 110.2, 110.8(d)3, 
150.0] Mandatory Requirements for Space-conditioning Equipment 
Exception 1 to Section 402.5.1.1: Existing inaccessible piping shall not require insulation as 
defined under Section 402.2.5 [Section 150.0(j)1]. 
Exception 2 to Section 402.5.1.1: When any length of duct is extended from an existing duct 
system to serve the addition, the existing duct system and the extended duct shall meet the 
applicable requirements specified in Section 402.5.2.2.5 [Section 150.2(b)1Di and 
150.2(b)1Dii]. 
Exception 3 to Section 402.5.1.1: Block loads, the total load for all rooms combined that are 
served by the central equipment, may be used to comply with Section 402.2.2.1 [Section 
150.0(h)1] for the purpose of system sizing for additions. 
402.5.1.2 [Section 150.2(a)1] Prescriptive requirements (Additions). 
Additions shall meet the requirements of Section 402.3 [Section 150.1(c)] and the applicable 
requirements of Sections 402.5.1.2.1 and 402.5.1.2.2. 
Exception to Section 402.5.1.2: Additions 1,000 square feet or less are not required to comply 
with the ventilation cooling requirements of Section 402.3.5 [Section 150.1(c)12]. 
402.5.1.2.1 [Section 150.2(a)1C] Mechanical ventilation for indoor air quality. 

Page 316 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 402 – SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES 
Additions to existing buildings shall comply with Sections 402.2.7 and 402.2.8 [Section 
150.0(o)] subject to the requirements specified below. 
Whole-dwelling unit mechanical ventilation. 
Dwelling units that meet the conditions in subsections 1, or 2 below shall not be required 
to comply with the whole-dwelling unit ventilation airflow specified in Section 402.2.7.3 
[Section 150.0(o)1C]. 
1. Additions to an existing dwelling unit that increase the conditioned floor area of the 
existing dwelling unit by less than or equal to 1000 square feet. 
2. Junior Accessory Dwelling Units (JADU) that are additions to an existing building. 
Additions to an existing dwelling unit that increase the conditioned floor area of the 
existing dwelling unit by more than 1,000 square feet shall have mechanical ventilation 
airflow in accordance with Section 402.2.7.3 [Section 150.0(o)1C] as applicable. The 
mechanical ventilation airflow rate shall be based on the conditioned floor area of the 
entire dwelling unit comprised of the existing dwelling unit conditioned floor area plus the 
addition conditioned floor area. 
New dwelling units that are additions to an existing building shall have mechanical 
ventilation airflow provided in accordance with Section 402.2.7.3 [Section 150.0(o)1C] as 
applicable. The mechanical ventilation airflow rate shall be based on the conditioned floor 
area of the new dwelling unit. 
Local mechanical exhaust. Additions to existing buildings shall comply with all applicable 
requirements specified in Section 402.2.7.5 [Section 150.0(o)1G] and Section 402.2.8 
[Section 150.0(o)2]. 
402.5.1.2.2 [Section 150.2(a)1E] Space-Conditioning load calculations and system 
capacity. 
402.5.1.2.2.1- Minimum capacity limits and supplemental heating requirements are as 
described in Section 402.2.2 [Section 150.0(h)]. 
402.5.1.2.2.2- The maximum capacity depends on the relative sizes of the calculated 
heating design load (HL) and cooling design load (CL), the type of space conditioning 
system, and the duct sizing. 
In situations where airflow is field verified to be at least 350 cfm/ton, there is no 
maximum capacity limit. 
In situations where airflow is NOT field verified to be at least 350 cfm/ton, the system 
capacities shall be no larger than indicated in Table 402.5-A [Table 150.2-A] for heating 
and Table 402.5-B [Table 150.2-B] for cooling. 
Exception 1 to Section 402.5.1.2.2.2: Ductless space-conditioning systems. 
Exception 2 to Section 402.5.1.2.2.2: For variable-speed and multi-speed systems, if 
the maximum system capacity specified in Tables 402.5-A or 402.5-B [Tables 150.2-A 
or 150.2-B] falls between two available system capacities for a space-conditioning 
system, the larger of the two available capacities may be selected.

Exception to Section 402.5.1.2.2.3: If leakage is established through field verification 
and diagnostic testing following procedures specified in Reference Residential

calculations and no disclosure is required.

402.5.1.3 [Section 150.2(a)2] Performance requirements (Additions). 
Performance calculations shall meet the requirements of Section 102 for the addition alone or 
for the existing building plus addition. 
Mechanical Ventilation for Indoor Air Quality. Additions to existing buildings shall comply 
with Sections 402.2.7 and 402.2.8 [Section 150.0(o)] subject to the requirements specified 
below: 
1. Whole-dwelling unit mechanical ventilation. Dwelling units that meet either conditions 
below shall not be required to comply with the whole-dwelling unit ventilation airflow 
specified in Section 402.2.7.3 [Section 150.0(o)1C]. 
1.1. Additions to an existing dwelling unit that increase the conditioned floor area of the 
existing dwelling unit by less than or equal to 1000 square feet. 
1.2. Junior Accessory Dwelling Units (JADU) that are additions to an existing building. 
Additions to an existing dwelling unit that increase the conditioned floor area of the 
existing dwelling unit by more than 1,000 square feet shall have mechanical ventilation 
airflow in accordance with Section 402.2.7.3 [Section 150.0(o)1C] as applicable. The 
mechanical ventilation airflow rate shall be based on the conditioned floor area of the 
entire dwelling unit comprised of the existing dwelling unit conditioned floor area plus the 
addition conditioned floor area. 
New dwelling units that are additions to an existing building shall have mechanical 
ventilation airflow provided in accordance with Section 402.2.7.3 [Section 150.0(o)1C] as 
applicable. The mechanical ventilation airflow rate shall be based on the conditioned floor 
area of the new dwelling unit. 
2. Local mechanical exhaust. Additions to existing buildings shall comply with all applicable 
requirements specified in Section 402.2.7.5 [Section 150.0(o)1G] and Section 402.2.8 
[Section 150.0(o)2].

402.5.2.2.3 [Section 150.2(b)1G] Altered space heating system. 
Altered or replacement space heating systems shall not use electric resistance as the 
primary heat source.

if the existing space heating system is electric resistance.

existing space heating system is electric resistance and the building is located in climate 
zones 7 or 15. 
402.5.2.2.4 [Section 150.2(b)1E] Altered space-conditioning system - duct sealing. 
In all climate zones, when a space-conditioning system serving a single-family dwelling is 
altered by the installation or replacement of space-conditioning system equipment, 
including replacement of the air handler, outdoor condensing unit of a split system air 
conditioner or heat pump, or cooling or heating coil; the duct system that is connected to 
the altered space-conditioning system equipment shall be sealed, as confirmed through 
field verification and diagnostic testing in accordance with the applicable procedures for 
duct sealing of altered existing duct systems as specified in Reference Residential 
Appendix RA3.1 and the leakage compliance criteria specified below. 
1. The measured duct leakage shall be equal to or less than 10 percent of system air 
handler airflow as determined utilizing the procedures in Reference Residential 
Appendix RA3.1.4.3.1; or 
2. The measured duct leakage to outside shall be equal to or less than 7 percent of 
system air handler airflow as determined utilizing the procedures in Reference 
Residential Appendix Section RA3.1.4.3.4; or 
3. If it is not possible to meet either of the duct leakage compliance criteria specified 
above, then, all accessible leaks shall be sealed and verified through a visual inspection 
and a smoke test by a certified ECC-Rater utilizing the methods specified in Reference 
Residential Appendix Section RA3.1.4.3.5. 
Additionally, when altered ducts, air-handling units, cooling or heating coils, or plenums 
are located in garage spaces, the system shall comply with Section 402.5.2.2.5.5 [Section 
150.2(b)1Diic] regardless of the length of any new or replacement space-conditioning 
ducts installed in the garage space. 
Exception 1 to Section 402.5.2.2.4: Duct systems that are documented to have been 
previously sealed as confirmed through field verification and diagnostic testing in 
accordance with procedures in the Reference Residential Appendix RA3.1.

duct system. If the new ducts form an entirely new or complete replacement duct

field verification and diagnostic testing utilizing the procedures in Reference 
Residential Appendix Section RA3.1.4.3.1.

consist of reused parts from the dwelling unit's existing duct system, including but not 
limited to registers, grilles, boots, air handler, coil, plenums, duct material; if the 
reused parts are accessible and can be sealed to prevent leakage. 
Entirely new or complete replacement duct systems shall also conform to the 
requirements of Sections 402.2.6.12 and 402.2.6.13 [Sections 150.0(m)12 and 
150.0(m)13]. If the air handler and ducts are located within a vented attic, the 
requirements of Section 302.5.2.2.4 [Section 150.2(b)1J] shall also be met.

402.5.2.2.5.4- Leakage compliance criteria - extension of an existing duct system. If 
the new ducts are an extension of an existing duct system serving single-family 
dwellings, the combined new and existing duct system shall meet one of the following 
requirements: 
1. The measured duct leakage shall be equal to or less than 10 percent of system air 
handler airflow as confirmed by field verification and diagnostic testing utilizing 
the procedures in Reference Residential Appendix Section RA3.1.4.3.1; or 
2. The measured duct leakage to outside shall be equal to or less than 7 percent of 
system air handler airflow as confirmed by field verification and diagnostic testing 
utilizing the procedures in Reference Residential Appendix Section RA3.1.4.3.4; or 
3. If it is not possible to meet either of the leakage compliance criteria specified 
above, then all accessible leaks shall be sealed and verified through a visual 
inspection and a smoke test by a certified ECC-Rater utilizing the methods 
specified in Reference Residential Appendix RA3.1.4.3.5. 
Exception to Section 402.5.2.2.5.4: Existing duct systems that are extended, which are 
constructed, insulated or sealed with asbestos. 
402.5.2.2.5.5- Leakage compliance criteria - altered ducts and duct system 
components in garage spaces. When new or replacement space-conditioning ducts, 
air-handling units, cooling or heating coils, or plenums are located in a garage space, 
compliance with either option below is required. 
1. The measured system duct leakage shall be less than or equal to 6 percent of 
system air handler airflow as determined utilizing the procedures in Reference 
Residential Appendix Section RA3.1.4.3.1; or 
2. All accessible leaks located in the garage space shall be sealed and verified through 
a visual inspection and a smoke test by a certified ECC-Rater utilizing the methods 
specified in Reference Residential Appendix RA3.1.4.3.5. 
402.5.2.2.6 [Section 150.2(b)1L] Mechanical ventilation for indoor air quality - 
entirely new or complete replacement ventilation Systems. 
Entirely new or complete replacement ventilation systems shall comply with all applicable 
requirements in Sections 402.2.7 and 402.2.8 [Section 150.0(o)]. An entirely new or 
complete replacement ventilation system includes a new ventilation fan component and 
an entirely new duct system. An entirely new or complete replacement duct system is 
constructed of at least 75 percent new duct material, and up to 25 percent may consist of 
reused parts from the dwelling unit's existing duct system, including but not limited to 
registers, grilles, boots, air filtration devices and duct material, if the reused parts are 
accessible and can be sealed to prevent leakage. 
402.5.2.2.7 [Section 150.2(b)1M] Mechanical ventilation for indoor air quality - 
altered ventilation systems. 
Altered ventilation system components or newly installed ventilation equipment serving 
the alteration shall comply with Sections 402.2.7 and 402.2.8 [Section 150.0(o)] as 
applicable subject to the requirements specified below.

402.5.2.2.7.1 [Section 150.2(b)1Mia] Whole-dwelling unit mechanical ventilation. 
If the whole-dwelling ventilation fan is altered or replaced, then one of the following

1. Dwellings that were required by a previous building permit to comply with the 
whole-dwelling unit airflow requirements in Sections 402.2.7 and 402.2.8 [Section

Additionally, when conformance to a specified whole-dwelling unit airflow rate is 
required for compliance, the replacement fans shall be rated at no less than the 
airflow rate required for compliance.

150.0(m)12] shall not be required to comply with the air filtration requirements 
specified in Section 402.2.6.12 [Section 150.0(m)12]. 
402.5.2.2.7.4 [Section 150.2(b)1Miia] Bathroom local mechanical exhaust.

requirements specified in Section 402.2.7.5 [Section 150.0(o)1G]. 
402.5.2.2.7.5 [Section 150.2(b)1Miib] Kitchen local mechanical exhaust.

SECTION 403 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
SECTION 403 
MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
(NEWLY CONSTRUCTED, ADDITIONS, ALTERATIONS) 
 
403.1 [Section 160.0] General. 
Multifamily building mechanical systems and equipment shall comply with the applicable 
requirements of Section403. Section 403 applies to dwelling units and common use areas in 
multifamily buildings. Nonresidential occupancies in a mixed occupancy building shall comply 
with nonresidential requirements in Section 401. 
NOTE: The requirements of Sections 403.2 through 403.4 apply to newly constructed buildings. 
Sections 403.2 and 403.5 apply to additions or alterations. 
 
403.2 [Section 160.2, 160.3] Mandatory requirements (Newly Constructed, Additions, 
Alterations). 
403.2.1 [Section 160.1(f)] Installation of fireplaces, decorative gas appliances and gas 
logs. 
Shall comply with Section 402.2.1. 
403.2.2 [Section 160.2] Mandatory requirements for ventilation and indoor air quality. 
Attached dwelling units in multifamily buildings shall comply with the applicable 
requirements of Sections 403.2.2.2 and 403.2.2.3 [Section 160.2(b)] below. Occupiable 
spaces in multifamily buildings other than attached dwelling units shall comply with the 
applicable requirements of Section 403.2.2.4 [Section 160.2(c)]. When field verification and 
diagnostic testing of attached dwelling units is required by Section 403.2.2 [Section 160.2], 
buildings with three habitable stories or fewer shall use the applicable procedures in the 
Residential Appendices, and buildings with four or more habitable stories shall use the 
applicable procedures in Nonresidential Appendices NA1 and NA2. 
NOTE: Section 403.2.2 [Section 160.2] is not applicable to townhouses or dwellings that 
contain two dwelling units. 
403.2.2.1 [Section 160.2(a)2] Compliance documentation. 
The required outdoor air-ventilation rate and the air-distribution system design shall be 
clearly identified on the building design plans submitted to the enforcement agency in 
accordance with Section 10-103 of Title 24, Part 1. 
403.2.2.2 [Section 160.2(b)1] Air filtration – Attached dwelling units.

Ventilation and Acceptable Indoor Air Quality in Residential Buildings subject to the 
amendments specified in Sections 403.2.2.3.1 through 403.2.2.3.11 [Section 160.2(b)2A]

Exception to Section 403.2.2.3: The following sections of ASHRAE 62.2 shall not be

4.3, Section 4.6, Section 5, Section 6.1.1, Section 6.1.3 and Normative Appendix A. 
403.2.2.3.1 [Section 160.2(b)2Ai] Window operation. 
Shall comply with Section 402.2.7.1.

Shall comply with Section 402.2.7.2.

403.2.2.3.4 [Section 160.2(b)2Aiv] Whole-dwelling unit mechanical ventilation. 
Multifamily attached dwelling units shall comply with requirements below: 
1. Mechanical ventilation airflow shall be provided at rates greater than or equal to 
the value determined in accordance with Equation 403.2-A [Equation 160.2-B]. 
Total Required Ventilation Rate [ASHRAE 62.2:4.1.1]. 
Qtot = 0.03Afloor + 7.5(Nbr + 1) (Equation 403.2-A [Equation 160.2-B]) 
where: 
Qtot = total required ventilation rate, cfm 
Afloor = dwelling unit floor area, ft
2 
Nbr = number of bedrooms (not to be less than 1) 
2. All dwelling units in a multifamily building shall use the same whole-dwelling unit 
ventilation system type. The dwelling unit shall comply with requirements below: 
2.1. Balanced or supply ventilation. A balanced or supply ventilation system shall 
provide the required whole-dwelling-unit ventilation airflow. Balanced 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 329 
SECTION 403 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
systems with heat recovery or energy recovery that serve a single dwelling 
unit shall have a fan efficacy of ≤1.0 W/cfm; and 
2.2. Compartmentalization Testing. The air leakage rate shall not exceed 0.3 
cubic feet per minute at 50 Pa (0.2 inch water) per ft2 of dwelling unit 
envelope surface area as confirmed by ECC-rater field verification and 
diagnostic testing in accordance with the procedures specified in Reference 
Appendix RA3.8 or NA2.3 as applicable. In multifamily buildings with four or 
more habitable stories, the field verification and diagnostic testing which 
requires an ECC-Rater may alternatively be performed by a certified 
Mechanical Acceptance Test Technician according to the requirements 
specified in Reference Appendix NA1.9. 
403.2.2.3.5 [Section 160.2(b)2Av] Central ventilation system airflow rate 
tolerance. 
1. Multifamily building central ventilation systems that serve multiple dwelling units 
shall have airflow rates in each dwelling unit served that meet or exceed a design 
ventilation airflow rate specification. 
2. Designers shall specify a design ventilation airflow rate for each dwelling unit that 
is equal to or greater than the rate specified by Equation 403.2-A [Equation 
160.2-B]. 
3. The design ventilation airflow rate for each dwelling unit shall be stated on the 
building design plans approved by the enforcement agency. 
4. Airflow in each dwelling unit shall be no more than twenty percent greater than 
the specified design ventilation airflow rate. Ventilation systems shall utilize 
mechanical or software airflow control means to ensure each of the dwelling unit 
airflows can be maintained at the design ventilation airflow within this tolerance 
at all times. System airflow control-means may include but are not limited to 
constant air regulation devices, orifice plates and variable speed central fans.

ventilation fan’s inlet terminals/grilles or outlet terminals/grilles in accordance with

for balanced systems. Balanced mechanical ventilation system airflow shall be the

1. The whole-dwelling unit ventilation airflow required by Section 403.2.2.3.4 or

[Section 160.2(b)2Avi], or alternatively the minimum capture efficiency as

2.2. The maximum sound rating as specified in Section 403.2.2.3.6.4 [Section 
160.2(b)2Avif].

fan efficacy. At a minimum, systems with heat or energy recovery serving a single

dwelling unit shall have a fan efficacy of ≤1.0 W/cfm as confirmed by field

403.2.2.3.13 [Section 160.2(b)2C] Central ventilation system field verification. 
Central ventilation system duct sealing. Ventilation ducts that meet the conditions 
below shall meet the duct sealing requirements in California Mechanical Code 
Section 603.10 and have leakage that is no greater than six percent of the rooftop 
fan or central fan design airflow rate as confirmed by field verification in accordance

conducted using a test pressure of 25 Pa (0.1 inches) for ducts serving six or fewer 
dwelling units and 50 Pa (0.2 inches) for ducts serving more than six dwelling units, 
and shall measure the leakage of all ductwork between the central fan and the 
connection point to the in-unit grille or fan. 
1. The ventilation ducts serve multiple dwelling units. 
2. The ventilation ducts provide continuous airflows or airflows to provide balanced 
ventilation to meet the requirements specified in Section 403.2.2.3.4 or 
403.2.2.3.5 [Section 160.2(b)2Aiv or 160.2(b)2Av] as applicable.

403.2.2.3.13 [Section 160.2(b)2C].

option. 
Ducts shall have a minimum installed level of R-6.0. 
Exception to Section 403.2.3.3.5.2: Portions of the duct system located in 
conditioned space below the ceiling separating the occupiable space from the 
attic are not required to be insulated if all of the following conditions are met: 
1. The noninsulated portion of the duct system is located entirely inside the 
building’s thermal envelope as confirmed by visual inspection. 
2. At all locations where noninsulated portions of the duct system penetrate 
into unconditioned space, the penetration shall be draft stopped compliant 
with CFC Sections 703.1 and 704.1 and air-sealed to the construction 
materials that are penetrated, using materials compliant with CMC Section 
E502.4.2 to prevent air infiltration into the cavity. All connections in 
unconditioned space are insulated to a minimum of R-6.0 as confirmed by 
visual inspection. 
403.2.3.3.5.3 [Section 160.3(b)5Aiib] CMC compliance - ducts in conditioned 
space option. 
1. Ducts do not require insulation when the duct system is located entirely in 
conditioned space. For buildings with three or fewer habitable stories, duct 
systems located entirely in conditioned space shall be confirmed through field 
verification and diagnostic testing in accordance with the requirements of 
Reference Residential Appendix RA3.1.4.3.8. 
2. Connections of metal ducts and the inner core of flexible ducts shall be 
mechanically fastened. 
3. Openings shall be sealed with mastic, tape, or other duct-closure system that 
meets the applicable requirements of UL 181, UL 181A or UL 181B or aerosol 
sealant that meets the requirements of UL 723. If mastic or tape is used to 
seal openings greater than 1/4 inch, the combination of mastic and either 
mesh or tape shall be used.

403.2.3.4.2.7 [Section 160.3(c)2Hi] Duct leakage testing. 
New duct systems that meet the criteria below or ductwork that is part of a 
system that meets the criteria of Sections 403.5.2.2.8 through 403.5.2.2.10 
[Section 180.2(b)2B] shall be sealed to a leakage rate not to exceed 6 percent of 
the nominal air handler airflow rate as confirmed through acceptance testing, in 
accordance with Reference Nonresidential Appendix NA7.5.3. 
1. The duct system provides conditioned air to an occupiable space for a 
constant volume, single zone, space-conditioning system; and 
2. The space-conditioning system serves less than 5,000 square feet of 
conditioned floor area; and 
3. The combined surface area of the ducts located in the following spaces is 
more than 25 percent of the total surface area of the entire duct system: 
3.1. Outdoors; or

403.3 [Section 170.2(c)] Prescriptive requirements (Newly Constructed) 
All space heating, space cooling and ventilation equipment shall comply with minimum 
Appliance Efficiency Regulations as specified in Sections 400.1 and 400.2 [Sections 110.0 
through 110.2] and the applicable requirements of this section. 
403.3.1 [Section 170.2(c)3] Space-conditioning systems - Dwelling units. 
403.3.1.1 [Section 170.2(c)3A] Heating system type. 
Space-conditioning systems serving dwelling units shall meet the applicable option 
below. Systems that cannot meet the requirements below, including multi-zone systems 
and systems using central boilers or chillers, shall comply with the performance 
requirements of Section 403.4 [Section 170.1]. 
1. Multifamily buildings three habitable stories or fewer. 
For Climate Zones 1 through 15, the space-conditioning system shall be a heat pump. 
For Climate Zone 16, the space-conditioning system shall be an air conditioner with 
furnace. Additionally, balanced ventilation systems serving these dwelling units shall 
meet the applicable requirements of Section 403.3.1.2.5 [Section 170.2(c)3Bv]. 
2. Multifamily buildings four habitable stories or greater. 
For Climate Zones 2 through 15, the space-conditioning system shall be a heat pump. 
For Climate Zones 1 and 16, the space-conditioning system shall be a dual-fuel heat 
pump. 
Exception to Section 403.3.1.1: A supplemental heating unit may be installed in a space 
served directly or indirectly by a primary heating system, provided that the unit thermal 

Page 344 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 403 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
capacity does not exceed 2 kW or 7,000 Btu/hr and is controlled by a time-limiting 
device not exceeding 30 minutes. 
403.3.1.2 [Section 170.2(c)3B] Space-conditioning and ventilation systems. 
All space heating and space cooling equipment serving dwelling units shall comply with 
all applicable requirements of this section. 
Exception to Section 403.3.1.2: The field verification and ECC-Provider data registry 
requirements of Reference Residential Appendix RA2 and RA3 are not required for 
multifamily dwelling units in buildings four habitable stories and greater. The installer 
shall certify that diagnostic testing was performed in accordance with the applicable 
procedures. 
403.3.1.2.1 [Section 170.2(c)3Bi] Refrigerant charge verification—systems 
serving individual dwelling units. 
Shall comply with the requirements of 402.3.2.1 with the following modification: 
In climate zones 2 and 8-15 air-cooled air conditioners and air-source heat pumps, 
including but not limited to ducted split systems, ducted packaged systems, small 
duct high velocity systems, and mini-split systems, shall comply with Section 
402.3.2.1.1 [Section 150.1(c)7Ai] unless the system is of a type that cannot be 
verified using the specified procedures. Systems which are of a type that cannot 
be verified using the specified procedures with the requirements of Section 
402.3.2.1.1 [Section 150.1(c)7Ai] shall comply with Section 402.3.2.1.2 [Section 
150.1(c)7Aii] as applicable. 
Exception to Section 403.3.1.2.1: The field verification and ECC-Provider data 
registry requirements of Reference Residential Appendix RA2 and RA3 are not 
required for multifamily dwelling units in buildings four habitable stories and greater. 
The installer shall certify that diagnostic testing was performed in accordance with 
the applicable procedures. 
403.3.1.2.2 [Section 170.2(c)3Bii] Space-conditioning distribution systems. 
All space-conditioning systems shall meet all applicable requirements of Section 
403.3.1.2.2.1 or Section 403.3.1.2.2.2. 
403.3.1.2.2.1 [Section 170.2(c)3Biia] High performance attics. 
Air handlers or ducts are allowed to be in ventilated attic spaces when the roof 
and ceiling insulation level meet Option B in Table 303.3-A [Table 170.2-A].

conditioned space. 
Duct systems and air handlers of HVAC systems shall be located in conditioned 
space, and confirmed by field verification and diagnostic testing to meet the 
criterion of Reference Residential Appendix RA3.1.4.3.8.

403.3.1.2.3 [Section 170.2(c)3Biii] Central fan integrated ventilation systems—
systems serving individual dwelling units. 
Central forced air system fans used to provide outside air shall have an air-handling 
unit fan efficacy less than or equal to the maximum W/cfm specified in one of the 
options below. 
1. 0.45 W/cfm for gas furnace air-handling units; or 
2. 0.58 W/cfm for air-handling units that are not gas furnaces. 
The airflow rate and fan efficacy requirements in this section shall be confirmed 
through field verification and diagnostic testing in accordance with all applicable 
procedures specified in Reference Residential Appendix RA3.3. Central Fan 
Integrated Ventilation Systems shall be certified to the Energy Commission as 
Intermittent Ventilation Systems as specified in Reference Residential Appendix 
RA3.7.4.2. 
403.3.1.2.4 [Section 170.2(c)3Biv] Balanced ventilation systems with 
heat/energy recovery in climate zones 1, 2, 4, 11-14, and 16. 
A balanced ventilation system with heat or energy recovery shall be used to meet 
Section 403.2.2.3.4 [Section 160.2(b)2Aivb1], and shall meet the applicable 
requirements below: 
403.3.1.2.4.1- In Climate Zones 1, 2, 4, 11-14, and 16, balanced ventilation 
systems serving individual dwelling units shall: 
1. Be an energy recovery ventilator (ERV) or heat recovery ventilator (HRV), 
2. Have a minimum sensible recovery efficiency of 67 percent, rated at 32 
degrees Fahrenheit (0 degrees Celsius), and 
3. Have a fan efficacy less than or equal to 0.6 W per cfm. 
These measures shall be confirmed through field verification in accordance with 
the procedures in RA3.7.4.4 for buildings with three habitable stories or less, or 
the procedures in NA2.2.4.1.5 for buildings with four or more habitable stories. 
403.3.1.2.4.2- In Climate Zones 1, 2, 4, 11-14, and 16, balanced ventilation 
systems serving multiple dwelling units in buildings with four or more habitable 
stories shall: 
1. Be an ERV or HRV, 
2. Have a minimum sensible recovery efficiency or effectiveness of 67 percent, 
rated at 32 degrees Fahrenheit (0 degrees Celsius), 

Page 346 (Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards 
SECTION 403 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
3. Meet the fan power requirements of Section 403.3.2.2 [Section 170.2(c)4A], 
and 
4. Have recovery bypass or control to directly economize with ventilation air 
based on outdoor air temperature limits specified in Table 401.3-G [Table 
170.2-G]. 
These measures shall be field verified in accordance with NA7.18.4. 
403.3.1.2.5 [Section 170.2(c)3Bv] Balanced ventilation system fan efficacy. 
In buildings with three habitable stories or less in Climate Zones 5–10 and Climate 
Zone 15, when a heat pump space-conditioning system is installed to meet the 
requirements of Section 403.3.1.1 [Section 170.2(c)3Ai], balanced ventilation systems 
without an ERV or HRV shall have a fan efficacy less than or equal to 0.4 W/cfm. 
403.3.1.2.6 [Section 170.2(c)3Bvi] Ventilation system Fault Indicator Display 
(FID). 
All HRV/ERV systems serving individual dwelling units shall have a Fault Indicator 
Display (FID) that is manufacturer certified in compliance with the requirements in 
Joint Appendix JA17.4. The FID certification shall be verified by an ECC-Rater. 
403.3.1.3 [Section 170.2(c)3C] HVAC system bypass ducts. 
Bypass ducts that deliver conditioned supply air directly to the space-conditioning 
system return duct airflow shall not be used per Section 402.3.6. 
403.3.2 [Section 170.2(c)4] Space-conditioning systems - Common use areas. 
A building complies with this section by being designed with and having constructed and 
installed a space-conditioning system that meets the applicable requirements of this section. 
403.3.2.1 [Section 170.2(c)1] Sizing and equipment selection. 
Mechanical heating and mechanical cooling equipment serving common use areas of 
multifamily buildings shall be the smallest size, within the available options of the 
desired equipment line, necessary to meet the design heating and cooling loads of the 
building, as calculated according to Section 403.3.2.1.1 below. 
Exception 1 to Section 403.3.2.1: Where it can be demonstrated to the satisfaction of 
the enforcing agency that oversizing will not increase building LSC energy use. 
Exception 2 to Section 403.3.2.1: Standby equipment with controls that allow the 
standby equipment to operate only when the primary equipment is not operating. 
Exception 3 to Section 403.3.2.1: Multiple units of the same equipment type, such as 
multiple chillers and boilers, having combined capacities exceeding the design load, if 
they have controls that sequence or otherwise optimally control the operation of each 
unit based on load.

is provided from a site-recovered or site-solar energy source. 
Exception 3 to Section 403.3.2.3: Zones in which specific humidity levels are required to 
satisfy non-covered process loads. Computer rooms or other spaces where the only 
process load is from IT equipment may not use this exception. 
Exception 4 to Section 403.3.2.3: Zones with a peak supply-air quantity of 300 cfm or 
less.

403.3.2.3.1 [Section 170.2(c)4Bi] Reheating, recooling, simultaneous heating and 
cooling. 
Each space-conditioning zone shall have controls that prevent: 
1. Reheating; and 
2. Recooling; and 
3. Simultaneous provisions of heating and cooling to the same zone, such as mixing 
or simultaneous supply of air that has been previously mechanically heated and 
air that has been previously cooled, either by cooling equipment or by 
economizer systems. 
403.3.2.3.2 [Section 170.2(c)4Bii] Zones served by VAV Systems. 
Zones served by variable air-volume systems that are designed and controlled to 
reduce, to a minimum, the volume of reheated, recooled, or mixed air are allowed 
only if the controls meet all of the following requirements: 
1. For each zone with direct digital controls (DDC): 
1.1. the volume of primary air that is reheated, recooled, or mixed air supply 
shall not exceed the larger of: 
1.1.1. 50 percent of the peak primary airflow; or 
1.1.2. The design zone outdoor airflow rate as specified for mechanical 
ventilation by Section 403.2.2.5 [Section 160.2(c)3]. 
1.2. The volume of primary air in the deadband shall not exceed the design 
zone outdoor airflow rate as specified for mechanical ventilation by 
Section 403.2.2.5 [Section 160.2(c)3]. 
1.3. The first stage of heating consists of modulating the zone supply air 
temperature setpoint up to a maximum setpoint no higher than 95 F 
degrees F while the airflow is maintained at the dead band flow rate. 
1.4. The second stage of heating consists of modulating the airflow rate from 
the dead band flow rate up to the heating maximum flow rate. 
2. For each zone without DDC: 
2.1. the volume of primary air that is reheated, re-cooled, or mixed air supply 
shall not exceed the larger of the following: 
2.1.1. 30 percent of the peak primary airflow; or 
2.1.2. The design zone outdoor airflow rate as specified for mechanical 
ventilation by Section 403.2.2.5 [Section 160.2(c)3].

403.3.2.6 [Section 170.2(c)4E] Electric-resistance heating. 
Electric-resistance heating systems shall not be used for space heating. 
Exception 1 to Section 403.3.2.6: Where an electric-resistance heating system 
supplements a heating system in which at least 60 percent of the annual energy 
requirement is supplied by site-solar or recovered energy. 
Exception 2 to Section 403.3.2.6: Where an electric-resistance heating system 
supplements a heat pump heating system, and the heating capacity of the heat pump is

403.3.2.1 [Section 170.2(c)1] at the design outdoor temperature specified in Section 
403.3.2.1.1 [Section 170.2(c)2]. 
Exception 3 to Section 403.3.2.6: Where the total capacity of all electric-resistance 
heating systems serving the entire building is less than 10 percent of the total design 
output capacity of all heating equipment serving the entire building. 
Exception 4 to Section 403.3.2.6: Where the total capacity of all electric-resistance 
heating systems serving the entire building, excluding those allowed under Exception 2, 
is no more than 3 kW. 
Exception 5 to Section 403.3.2.6: Heating systems serving as emergency backup to gas 
heating equipment.

403.3.2.15.1 [Section 170.2(c)4Oi] Sensible energy recovery ratio/ Enthalpy 
recovery ratio. 
A sensible energy recovery ratio of at least 60 percent or an enthalpy recovery ratio 
of at least 50 percent for both heating and cooling design conditions. 
Exception 1 to Section 403.3.2.15.1: Sensible recovery ratio requirements at heating 
design conditions are not required for Climate Zone 15. 
Exception 2 to Section 403.3.2.15.1: Sensible recovery ratio requirements at cooling 
design conditions are not required for Climate Zone 1. 
403.3.2.15.2 [Section 170.2(c)4Oii] Energy recovery bypass/ control. 
Shall comply with the requirements of 401.3.18.2. 
403.3.2.15.3 [Section 170.2(c)4Oiii] Design supply fan airflow rate. 
For a DOAS unit and a separate independent space-conditioning system meeting the 
requirements of Section 170.2(c)4Nia, the design supply fan airflow rate shall be the 
total airflow of only the DOAS unit.

403.4 [Section 100.2] Performance requirements (Newly Constructed). 
A building complies with the performance standards compliance approach as described in 
Section 102 if the energy consumption calculated for the proposed design building is no greater 
than the energy budget calculated for the standard design building using Commission-certified 
compliance software as specified by the Alternative Calculation Methods Reference Manual. 
 
403.5 [Sections 180.1, 180.2] Additions and alterations to existing buildings. 
403.5.1 [Section 180.1] Additions. 
Additions to existing multifamily buildings shall meet the mandatory requirements of 
Section 403.5.1.1, and either prescriptive requirements of Section 403.5.1.2 [Section 
180.1(a)] or performance requirements of Section 403.5.1.3 [Section 180.1(b)]. 
Exception 1 to Section 403.5.1: When heating or cooling will be extended to an addition 
from the existing system(s), the existing heating and cooling equipment need not comply 
with Part 6. The heating system capacity must be adequate to meet the minimum 
requirements of CBC Section 1204.1. 
Exception 2 to Section 403.5.1: When any length of duct is extended from an existing duct 
system to serve the addition, the existing duct system and the extended duct shall meet the 
applicable requirements specified in Section 403.5.2.2.1 and Section 403.5.2.2.5 [Sections 
180.2(b)2Ai and 180.2(b)2Aii]. 
Exception 3 to Section 403.5.1: New or replacement space heating systems serving a 
dwelling unit in an addition may be a heat pump or gas heating system.

403.5.2 [Section 180.2] Alterations. 
Alterations to components of existing multifamily buildings, including alterations made in 
conjunction with a change in building occupancy to a multifamily occupancy, shall meet 
mandatory requirements of Section 403.5.2.1, and either prescriptive requirements of 
Section 403.5.2.2 or performance requirements of Section 403.5.2.3. 
Exception 1 to Section 403.5.2: When heating or cooling for an alteration is provided by 
expanding existing systems, the existing systems and equipment need not comply with 
Sections 400.1 through 400.5, 403.1 through 403.2.3 and 403.3. 
Exception 2 to Section 403.5.2: When existing heating or cooling systems or components 
are moved within a building, the existing systems or components need not comply with 
Sections 400.1 through 400.5, 403.1 through 403.2.3 and 403.3. 
Exception 3 to Section 403.5.2: Where an existing system with electric reheat is expanded 
when adding variable air volume (VAV) boxes to serve an alteration, total electric reheat 
capacity may be expanded not to exceed 20 percent of the existing installed electric capacity 
in any one permit and the system need not comply with Section 403.3.2.6 [Section 
170.2(c)4E]. Additional electric reheat capacity in excess of 20 percent may be added subject 
to the requirements of Section 403.3.2.6 [Section 170.2(c)4E].

403.5.2.2.4 [Section 180.2(b)2Aiii] Altered space-conditioning system—duct 
sealing – Dwelling units. 
In all climate zones, when a space-conditioning system serving a multifamily dwelling 
is altered by the installation or replacement of space-conditioning system equipment, 
including replacement of the air handler, outdoor condensing unit of a split system 
air conditioner or heat pump, or cooling or heating coil, the duct system that is 
connected to the altered space-conditioning system equipment shall be sealed, as 
confirmed through field verification and diagnostic testing in accordance with the 
applicable procedures for duct sealing of altered existing duct systems as specified in 
Reference Residential Appendix RA3.1 and the leakage compliance criteria specified 
below. 
1. The measured duct leakage shall be equal to or less than 15 percent of air 
handler airflow as determined utilizing the procedures in Reference Residential 
Appendix Section RA3.1.4.3.1; or 
2. The measured duct leakage to outside shall be equal to or less than 10 percent of 
air handler airflow as determined utilizing the procedures in Reference 
Residential Appendix Section RA3.1.4.3.4; or

3. If it is not possible to meet the leakage compliance criteria of either one or two 
specified above, then all accessible leaks shall be sealed and verified through a

specified in Reference Residential Appendix RA3.1.4.3.5. 
Exception 1 to Section 403.5.2.2.4: Duct systems that are documented to have been 
previously sealed as confirmed through field verification and diagnostic testing in 
accordance with procedures in Reference Residential Appendix RA3.1. 
Exception 2 to Section 403.5.2.2.4: Duct systems with less than 40 linear feet as

403.5.2.2.5.3- Leakage compliance criteria - entirely new or complete 
replacement duct system. 
1. If the new ducts form an entirely new or complete replacement duct system 
directly connected to the air handler, the duct system shall meet one of the 
following requirements: 
1.1. The total leakage of the duct system shall not exceed 12 percent of the 
air handler airflow as determined utilizing the procedures in Reference 
Residential Appendix Section RA3.1.4.3.1, or 
1.2. The duct system leakage to outside shall not exceed 6 percent of the air 
handler airflow as determined utilizing the procedures in Reference 
Residential Appendix Section RA3.1.4.3.4. 
2. Entirely new or complete replacement duct systems installed as part of an 
alteration are constructed of at least 75 percent new duct material, and up to 
25 percent may consist of reused parts from the dwelling unit's existing duct 
system, including but not limited to registers, grilles, boots, air handler, coil, 
plenums and duct material, if the reused parts are accessible and can be 
sealed to prevent leakage. 
3. Entirely new or complete replacement duct systems shall also conform to the 
requirements of Section 403.2.2 [Section 160.2(a)1] and Section 403.2.3.3.9 
[Section 160.3(b)5L]. If the air handler and ducts are located within a vented 
attic, the requirements of Section 303.5.2.2.2 [Section 180.2(b)1Bi] shall also 
be met. 
403.5.2.2.5.4- Leakage compliance criteria - extension of an existing duct 
system. If the new ducts are an extension of an existing duct system serving 
multifamily dwellings, the combined new and existing duct system shall meet one 
of the following requirements: 
1. The measured duct leakage shall be equal to or less than 15 percent of air 
handler airflow as confirmed by field verification and diagnostic testing 
utilizing the procedures in Reference Residential Appendix Section 
RA3.1.4.3.1; or 
2. The measured duct leakage to outside shall be equal to or less than 10 
percent of air handler airflow as confirmed by field verification and diagnostic 
testing utilizing the procedures in Reference Residential Appendix Section 
RA3.1.4.3.4; or 
3. If it is not possible to meet the duct sealing requirements of either one or two 
specified above, then all accessible leaks shall be sealed and verified through 
a visual inspection and a smoke test by a certified ECC-Rater utilizing the 
methods specified in Reference Residential Appendix RA3.1.4.3.5. 
Exception to Section 403.5.2.2.5.4: Existing duct systems that are extended, 
which are constructed, insulated or sealed with asbestos.

403.3.2 [Sections 170.2(c)1, 2, and 4], applicable to the systems or components being 
altered. 
For compliance with Section 403.3.2.2 [Section 170.2(c)4A], additional fan power 
adjustment credits are available as specified in Table 403.5-B [TABLE 180.2-D]. 
Exception 1 to Section 403.5.2.2.8: Section 403.5.2.2.3 [Section 180.2(b)2Av] does 
not apply to replacement of electric reheat of equivalent or lower capacity electric 
resistance space heaters when natural gas is not available. 
Exception 2 to Section 403.5.2.2.8: Operable wall or roof openings that have been 
previously installed without interlock controls are exempt from complying with 
Section 403.3.2.12 [Section 170.2(c)4L]. 
Exception 3 to Section 403.5.2.2.8: Section 403.3.2.4 [Section 170.2(c)4Ci] is not 
applicable to systems that meet both of the following: 
1. The system is not a single package air-cooled commercial unitary air conditioner 
or heat pump; and 
2. The cooling capacity of the system is less than 54,000 Btu/h.

403.5.2.2.9 [Section 180.2(b)2Bii] Altered duct systems – Common use areas. 
When new or replacement space-conditioning system ducts are installed to serve an 
existing building, the new ducts shall meet the requirements of Section 403.2.3.4.2 
[Section 160.3(c)2] and the requirements below: 
403.5.2.2.9.1 [Section 180.2(b)2Biib] New or replacement duct systems. 
Entirely new or replacement duct systems installed as part of an alteration shall 
be leakage-tested in accordance with Section 403.2.3.4.2.7 [Section 160.3(c)2H]. 
Entirely new or replacement duct systems installed as part of an alteration shall 
be constructed of at least 75 percent new duct material, and up to 25 percent 
may consist of reused parts from the building's existing duct system, including 
registers, grilles, boots, air handlers, coils, plenums, and ducts, if the reused parts 
are accessible and can be sealed to prevent leakage. 
Exception 1 to Section 403.5.2.2.9.1: When it is not possible to achieve the duct 
leakage criteria in Section 403.5.2.2.9.1 [Section 180.2(b)2Biib], all accessible 
leaks shall be sealed and verified through a visual inspection and a smoke test 
performed by a certified mechanical acceptance test technician utilizing the 
methods specified in Reference Nonresidential Appendix NA7.5.3. 
Exception 2 to 403.5.2.2.9.1: Duct Sealing. Existing duct systems that are 
extended, which are constructed, insulated or sealed with asbestos are not 
required to comply with Section 403.5.2.2.9.1 [Section 180.2(b)2Biib]. 
403.5.2.2.9.2 [Section 180.2(b)2Biic] Extension of existing duct systems. 
If the new ducts are an extension of an existing duct system and the combined 
new and existing duct system meets the criteria below, the duct system shall be 
sealed to a leakage rate not to exceed 15 percent of the nominal air handler 
airflow rate as confirmed through acceptance testing, in accordance with 
Reference Nonresidential Appendix NA7.5.3: 
1. The duct system provides conditioned air to an occupiable space for a 
constant volume, single zone, space-conditioning system; and 
2. The space conditioning system serves less than 5,000 square feet of 
conditioned floor area; and 
3. The combined surface area of the ducts located in the following spaces is 
more than 25 percent of the total surface area of the entire duct system: 
3.1. Outdoors; 
3.2. In a space directly under a roof that: 
Has a U-factor greater than the U-factor of the ceiling, or if the roof does 
not meet the requirements of Section 303.3.1.1.2 [Section 170.2(a)1B], 
or 
Has fixed vents or openings to the outside or unconditioned spaces; or 

(Restructured) 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards Page 365 
SECTION 403 – MULTIFAMILY OCCUPANCIES 
3.3. In an unconditioned crawl space; or 
3.4. In other unconditioned spaces. 
403.5.2.2.10 [Section 180.2(b)2Biii] Altered space-conditioning systems – 
Common use areas. 
Space-conditioning systems altered by the installation or replacement of space-
conditioning system equipment (including replacement of the air handler, outdoor 
condensing unit of a split system air conditioner or heat pump, or cooling or heating 
coil) shall meet the requirements below: 
403.5.2.2.10.1 [Section 180.2(b)2Biiia] Demand responsive thermostat. 
1. For all altered units where the existing thermostat does not comply with the 
requirements for demand responsive controls specified in Section 400.6 
[Section 110.12], the existing thermostat shall be replaced with a demand 
responsive thermostat that complies with Section 400.6 [Section 110.12]. 
2. All newly installed space-conditioning systems requiring a thermostat shall be 
equipped with a demand responsive thermostat that complies with Section 
400.6 [Section 110.12]. 
403.5.2.2.10.2 [Section 180.2(b)2Biiib] Duct sealing. 
The duct system that is connected to the new or replaced space-conditioning 
system equipment shall be sealed, if the duct system meets the criteria of Section 
401.2.4.7 [Section 120.4(g)], as confirmed through acceptance testing, in 
accordance with the applicable procedures for duct sealing of altered existing 
duct systems as specified in Reference Nonresidential Appendix NA7.5.3, and 
conforming to the applicable leakage compliance criteria in Section 403.5.2.2.9 
[Section 180.2(b)2Bii]. 
Exception 1 to Section 403.5.2.2.10.2: Buildings altered so that the duct system 
no longer meets the criteria of Section 403.2.3.4.2.7 [Section 160.3(c)2Hi] are not 
required to comply with Section 403.5.2.2.10.2 [Section 180.2(b)2Biiib]. 
Exception 2 to Section 403.5.2.2.10.2: Duct systems that are documented to 
have been previously sealed as confirmed through acceptance testing in 
accordance with procedures in the Reference Nonresidential Appendix NA7.5.3 
are not required to comply with Section 403.5.2.2.10.2 [Section 180.2(b)2Biiib]. 
Exception 3 to Section 403.5.2.2.10.2: Existing duct systems constructed, 
insulated or sealed with asbestos are not required to comply with the 
requirements of Section 403.5.2.2.10.2 [Section 180.2(b)2Biiib]. 
403.5.2.3 [Sections 180.2(c)] Performance requirements (Alterations). 
The altered component(s) and any newly installed equipment serving the alteration shall 
meet the applicable requirements of Section 102.
